diamond_model_summary: The TCLBANKER incident involves a sophisticated adversary, Water Saci, targeting Brazilian financial institutions. The adversary employs advanced capabilities such as DLL side-loading and environment-gated payload decryption. The infrastructure includes C2 servers and propagation mechanisms via WhatsApp and Outlook. Victims are primarily in the financial sector in Brazil, with high impact severity due to data theft and social engineering tactics.
doc_summary: TCLBANKER is a Brazilian banking trojan capable of targeting 59 banking, fintech, and cryptocurrency platforms. Tracked by Elastic Security Labs as REF3076, it is a major update of the Maverick malware, which uses the SORVEPOTEL worm to spread via WhatsApp Web. The attack chain involves a loader with anti-analysis capabilities deploying a banking trojan and a worm component. The malware abuses a signed Logitech program for DLL side-loading, executing only if loaded by specific executables. It generates fingerprints for anti-debugging and anti-virtualization checks, ensuring execution on Brazilian systems. TCLBANKER establishes persistence, communicates with external servers, and uses a URL monitor to target financial institutions. It employs social engineering tactics for data theft and propagates via WhatsApp and Outlook. The campaign reflects a maturation in the Brazilian banking trojan ecosystem, using sophisticated techniques like environment-gated payload decryption and WebSocket command dispatch.
kill_chain_summary: The TCLBANKER attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with weaponization through a malicious MSI installer. Delivery is achieved via DLL side-loading, exploiting a signed Logitech program. Installation involves persistence through scheduled tasks. Command and control are maintained via HTTP POST requests, while actions on objectives include data theft and social engineering using full-screen overlays. The campaign reflects a maturation in the Brazilian banking trojan ecosystem.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered fraudulent apps on Google Play Store claiming to offer call history access, tricking users into subscriptions with fake data, causing financial loss. The apps, named CallPhantom by ESET, targeted Android users in India and Asia-Pacific, amassing over 7.3 million downloads before removal. The apps falsely claimed to provide call, SMS, and WhatsApp logs, requiring payment for access, but delivered fabricated data. Payments were made via Google Play billing, UPI, and direct card entry, violating Google's policy. The apps had simple interfaces, requested no sensitive permissions, and lacked functionality to retrieve actual data. Users who subscribed via Google Play may be eligible for refunds, while others depend on external providers. The incident highlights the need for vigilance against fraudulent apps exploiting trusted platforms.

Title: High-Severity Vulnerabilities in Next.js Addressed by Vercel

Victim.Description: Developers and organizations using Next.js versions 13.x to 16.x

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves high-severity vulnerabilities in Next.js versions 13.x to 16.x, affecting web applications using the React framework. The vulnerabilities include unauthenticated Denial of Service (DoS), Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), and middleware authentication bypasses. Exploits such as CVE-2026-44575 and CVE-2026-44578 are used to target App Router setups and self-hosted Next.js applications. Vercel has released patches in versions 15.5.16 and 16.2.5 to mitigate these threats.
doc_summary: Vercel has released critical security updates for Next.js to address high-severity vulnerabilities affecting versions 13.x to 16.x. These vulnerabilities, disclosed by Tim Neutkens via GitHub advisories, include unauthenticated Denial of Service (DoS), Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), and middleware authentication bypasses. Key CVEs include CVE-2026-44575, CVE-2026-44574, CVE-2026-44573, CVE-2026-23870, CVE-2026-44579, and CVE-2026-44578. The patches are available in versions 15.5.16 and 16.2.5. Developers are urged to update their Next.js packages to secure their environments. For those unable to patch immediately, Vercel recommends blocking specific headers and enforcing authorization within page logic. The vulnerabilities impact App Router setups, Pages Router with internationalization, and self-hosted Next.js applications using Node.js servers. Vercel-hosted deployments are unaffected by the SSRF flaw. The broader Next.js 16.2 release also includes performance enhancements and over 200 Turbopack fixes.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting vulnerabilities in Next.js to bypass authentication and perform DoS attacks. The exploitation stage is critical, with tactics such as Initial Access and techniques like Exploit Public-Facing Application being employed. Detection involves monitoring HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrade requests, while remediation includes updating Next.js and blocking specific headers.

Title: Dirty Frag: New Linux Kernel Vulnerability Exploit

Victim.Description: Major Linux distributions including Ubuntu, RHEL, Fedora, CentOS Stream, AlmaLinux, and openSUSE are affected.

diamond_model_summary: The Dirty Frag exploit represents a significant threat to Linux systems, leveraging two page-cache write vulnerabilities to achieve local privilege escalation. The xfrm-ESP and RxRPC vulnerabilities are chained to bypass system protections, affecting major Linux distributions. Mitigation involves blocking specific kernel modules.
doc_summary: A new Linux kernel vulnerability class, Dirty Frag, has been disclosed, allowing local privilege escalation across major Linux distributions. The exploit manipulates the kernel's page cache, enabling attackers to gain root access without write permissions on disk files. Two vulnerabilities, xfrm-ESP and RxRPC Page-Cache Write, are chained to bypass protections. The xfrm-ESP flaw exists in the IPsec stack since 2017, while RxRPC was introduced in 2023. The exploit affects Ubuntu, RHEL, Fedora, CentOS Stream, AlmaLinux, and openSUSE. Mitigation involves blocking esp4, esp6, and rxrpc kernel modules. No official patches are available yet.
kill_chain_summary: The Dirty Frag exploit follows a structured attack path, beginning with the weaponization of two Linux kernel vulnerabilities. The exploitation phase involves manipulating the page cache to gain root access, while actions on objectives include modifying system files. Mitigation strategies focus on blocking vulnerable kernel modules.

Title: Critical Vulnerability in Rancher Fleet: CVE-2026-41050

Victim.Description: Organizations using vulnerable versions of Rancher Fleet for Kubernetes management.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in Rancher Fleet, identified as CVE-2026-41050, which allows attackers to bypass multi-tenant isolation and escalate privileges. The adversary exploits the Helm deployer to gain unauthorized access to sensitive data. The infrastructure affected includes Kubernetes clusters managed by vulnerable Rancher Fleet versions. Victims are organizations using these versions, primarily in the technology sector.
doc_summary: The SUSE Rancher Security team disclosed a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-41050, affecting Rancher Fleet, a GitOps tool for Kubernetes cluster management. This flaw compromises the multi-tenant isolation mechanism, allowing attackers to bypass security boundaries and steal sensitive data. The vulnerability is due to the Helm deployer's failure to enforce ServiceAccount impersonation, enabling privilege escalation to cluster-admin status. Attackers can exploit the Helm lookup function and FleetFleet.yaml configuration file to extract admin tokens and credentials. Affected versions include Rancher Fleet before 0.11.13, 0.12.14, 0.13.10, and 0.14.5, and Rancher 2.10.11 and older. Immediate patching and security measures are recommended.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of a vulnerability in Rancher Fleet's Helm deployer, allowing attackers to bypass security boundaries. This leads to privilege escalation and unauthorized access to sensitive data. The adversary uses the Helm lookup function and FleetFleet.yaml configuration file to extract admin tokens and credentials. The attack impacts Kubernetes clusters managed by vulnerable Rancher Fleet versions, requiring immediate patching and security measures.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new Linux backdoor named PamDOORa, advertised on the Rehub Russian cybercrime forum for $1,600 by a threat actor called darkworm. The backdoor is designed as a Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM)-based post-exploitation toolkit that enables persistent SSH access via a magic password and specific TCP port combination. It can harvest credentials from legitimate users who authenticate through the compromised system. PamDOORa is the second Linux backdoor targeting the PAM stack after Plague. PAM is a security framework in Unix/Linux operating systems that allows system administrators to incorporate multiple authentication mechanisms. The pam_exec module can be exploited by attackers to gain unauthorized access or establish persistent control. PamDOORa incorporates anti-forensic capabilities to tamper with authentication logs. The malware's initial asking price was $1,600, reduced to $900 by April 9, 2026.
kill_chain_summary: The PamDOORa backdoor follows a kill chain involving weaponization through the development of a PAM-based toolkit, installation via PAM module manipulation, and actions on objectives including credential harvesting and anti-forensic log tampering. Title: Dirty Frag: New Linux Kernel Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

Victim.Description: Linux distributions affected by the Dirty Frag vulnerability.

diamond_model_summary: The Dirty Frag vulnerability represents a significant threat to Linux systems, allowing local privilege escalation. The adversary can exploit this vulnerability by chaining the xfrm-ESP and RxRPC Page-Cache Write vulnerabilities. The capability to exploit this vulnerability is high, given the deterministic nature of the bug. The infrastructure primarily involves Linux distributions, and the victims are systems running affected Linux kernels. The impact severity is high due to the potential for gaining root access.
doc_summary: A new local privilege escalation vulnerability named Dirty Frag has been identified in the Linux kernel. It is considered a successor to Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431) and allows unprivileged local users to gain root access on various Linux distributions, including Ubuntu 24.04.4, RHEL 10.1, openSUSE Tumbleweed, CentOS Stream 10, AlmaLinux 10, and Fedora 44. The vulnerability exploits the xfrm-ESP Page-Cache Write and RxRPC Page-Cache Write vulnerabilities. The xfrm-ESP vulnerability was introduced in a 2017 commit, while the RxRPC vulnerability appeared in 2023. The exploit requires creating a namespace, which is blocked by Ubuntu's AppArmor, but RxRPC can be used on systems where the rxrpc.ko module is loaded by default. A proof-of-concept has been released, and until patches are available, it is advised to blocklist esp4, esp6, and rxrpc modules.
kill_chain_summary: The Dirty Frag vulnerability follows a typical exploitation kill chain. The adversary gains initial access through local privilege escalation by exploiting the vulnerability. The exploitation stage is critical, as it allows the adversary to gain root privileges on affected Linux systems. Detection involves monitoring for unusual process creation and unauthorized namespace creation attempts. Remediation includes blocklisting vulnerable modules and applying patches once available. The vulnerability's deterministic nature increases the likelihood of successful exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the Dirty Frag vulnerability includes several key indicators. The exploit involves specific vulnerabilities (xfrm-ESP and RxRPC Page-Cache Write), which are challenging to detect and remediate. The lack of specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names makes detection more difficult. However, monitoring for unusual process activities and unauthorized namespace creation can help identify exploitation attempts. The high impact of the vulnerability on Linux systems underscores the need for effective detection and remediation strategies.

doc_summary: TCLBanker is a new trojan targeting 59 banking, fintech, and cryptocurrency platforms, primarily in Brazil. It uses a trojanized MSI installer for Logitech AI Prompt Builder to infect systems. The malware includes self-spreading worm modules for WhatsApp and Outlook, allowing it to propagate autonomously. TCLBanker is believed to be an evolution of the Maverick/Sorvepotel malware family. It features environment-dependent payload decryption routines and a persistent watchdog thread to evade analysis. The malware is loaded via DLL side-loading within the legitimate Logitech application, avoiding detection by security products. The banking module monitors browser activity and establishes a WebSocket session with the C2 server for remote control operations. TCLBanker uses a WPF-based overlay system to steal data and propagate to contacts through hijacked WhatsApp and Outlook accounts.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new credential theft framework named PCPJack, which targets exposed cloud infrastructure and removes artifacts linked to TeamPCP. The toolset harvests credentials from cloud, container, developer, productivity, and financial services, exfiltrating data through attacker-controlled infrastructure while spreading to additional hosts. PCPJack targets cloud services like Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, MongoDB, RayML, and vulnerable web applications, allowing operators to spread in a worm-like fashion and move laterally within compromised networks. The campaign aims to generate illicit revenue through credential theft, fraud, spam, extortion, or resale of stolen access. PCPJack shares significant targeting overlaps with TeamPCP, a threat actor known for exploiting security vulnerabilities and misconfigurations in cloud services. PCPJack lacks a cryptocurrency mining component, unlike TeamPCP, suggesting it could be the work of a former TeamPCP member. The attack starts with a bootstrap shell script that prepares the environment, downloads next-stage tooling, and removes TeamPCP artifacts. Six Python payloads are used, with propagation targets pulled from Common Crawl. The threat actor's infrastructure includes a shell script that detects CPU architecture and fetches the appropriate Sliver binary, scanning for credentials associated with various services and transmitting them to an external server.
kill_chain_summary: PCPJack follows a structured attack chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify exposed cloud services, followed by weaponization and delivery of payloads via a bootstrap shell script. Exploitation of vulnerabilities allows for installation of Python scripts, establishing persistence. Cloud environments require immediate access to audit logs and configurations to prevent loss of ephemeral telemetry. Title: Fake Claude AI Website Distributes Beagle Backdoor via Malicious Claude-Pro Relay

Victim.Description: Users who download the malicious Claude-Pro Relay from the fake Claude AI website
Victim.Security_Posture: Compromised if NOVupdate files are present

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a fake Claude AI website distributing a malicious Claude-Pro Relay download, which installs the Beagle backdoor and PlugX malware. The adversary uses a fake website to mimic the legitimate Claude AI site, delivering a trojanized installer. The Beagle backdoor communicates with a C2 server hosted on Alibaba-Cloud, using TCP and UDP protocols. The campaign may be linked to PlugX operators experimenting with new payloads.
doc_summary: A fake version of the Claude AI website offers a malicious Claude-Pro Relay download, pushing a previously undocumented backdoor for Windows named Beagle. The threat actor advertises Claude-Pro as a high-performance relay service for Claude-Code developers. The fake website mimics the legitimate site for the popular Claude large language model and AI assistant. Users landing on claude-pro[.]com can only click on a large download button for the malicious resource, a 505MB archive named 'Claude-Pro-windows-x64.zip' containing an MSI installer. Sophos reports that running the binary adds three files to the Startup folder: NOVupdate.exe, NOVupdate.exe.dat, and avk.dll. The 'Pro' installer is a trojanized copy of Claude that deploys a PlugX malware chain, giving attackers remote access. The first-stage payload is DonutLoader, fetching a simple backdoor called Beagle. The Beagle backdoor is distinct from the Delphi-based Beagle/Bagle worm. The campaign uses a signed updater for G Data security solutions to sideload the malicious DLL and encrypted file. The DLL decrypts and executes the payload in memory using DonutLoader. The backdoor communicates with the C2 at license[.]claude-pro[.]com using TCP over port 443 and/or UDP over port 8080, protected by a hardcoded AES key. The C2 is hosted at 8.217.190[.]58, associated with Alibaba-Cloud service. Additional samples related to Beagle were submitted to VirusTotal, using the same XOR decryption key. The campaign may be linked to PlugX operators experimenting with a new payload. Users should download Claude from the official portal and avoid sponsored search results. The presence of NOVupdate files indicates compromise.
kill_chain_summary: The adversary conducts reconnaissance to create a fake Claude AI website, weaponizes the Claude-Pro Relay installer with the Beagle backdoor and PlugX malware, and delivers it via the fake site. The installer is executed, installing the malware on the victim's system. The Beagle backdoor communicates with a C2 server using TCP and UDP protocols, allowing the adversary to gain remote access. The campaign uses sideloading and in-memory execution for persistence and evasion.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses, domain names, and malware filenames. The adversary uses a fake website and C2 infrastructure hosted on Alibaba-Cloud. The Beagle backdoor and PlugX malware are key components of the attack. The adversary employs sideloading and in-memory execution techniques to evade detection. The presence of NOVupdate files on a system indicates compromise. The campaign may be linked to PlugX operators experimenting with new payloads.

doc_summary: A phishing campaign is targeting ManageWP credentials through Google sponsored search results. The threat actor employs an adversary-in-the-middle approach, using a fake login page as a real-time proxy between victims and the legitimate ManageWP service. ManageWP is a platform for managing WordPress websites, commonly used by web developers, agencies, and enterprises. The fake search result appears above the real one for 'managewp' queries, leading users to a malicious login page. Credentials entered are sent to a Telegram channel controlled by the attacker. The campaign uses a live AiTM setup, allowing attackers to log into the platform in real-time. Victims are prompted to enter a 2FA code, which is used to access the ManageWP account. Guardio Labs researchers infiltrated the attacker's C2 infrastructure, observing a dropdown command system for interactive phishing. The phishing framework includes a Russian-language agreement disclaiming illegal activity responsibility and prohibiting leaks or use against Russia-based systems. Guardio Labs has contacted 200 unique victims to alert them about the exposure.

Weaponization involves creating a phishing framework with real-time proxy capabilities. Delivery is executed through Google sponsored search results, leading victims to a fake login page. Command and control is maintained via Telegram, while actions on objectives involve accessing ManageWP accounts and potentially controlling WordPress sites. doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a new Mirai-derived botnet named xlabs_v1, which targets internet-exposed devices running Android Debug Bridge (ADB) to conduct distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. The botnet, discovered by Hunt.io, operates from a Netherlands-hosted server at IP address 176.65.139.44 and is offered as a DDoS-for-hire service targeting game servers and Minecraft hosts. It exploits devices with ADB enabled by default, such as Android TV boxes and IoT hardware, and uses a bandwidth-tiered pricing model. The botnet lacks persistence mechanisms, requiring re-infection for each attack. The threat actor, known as Tadashi, employs a killer subsystem to eliminate competitors and maximize bandwidth usage. The infrastructure also includes a Monero-mining toolkit, suggesting potential links to other malicious activities.
kill_chain_summary: The xlabs_v1 botnet follows a structured attack chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify devices with exposed ADB services. It then weaponizes payloads for multiple architectures and delivers them via ADB-shell pastes. The botnet exploits devices with ADB enabled by default, installs malware, and communicates with a C2 server for instructions. Finally, it executes DDoS attacks on game servers.

doc_summary: The Iranian state-sponsored hacking group MuddyWater, also known as Mango Sandstorm, Seedworm, and Static Kitten, has been linked to a ransomware attack described as a false flag operation. The attack, observed by Rapid7 in early 2026, utilized social engineering techniques via Microsoft Teams to initiate the infection sequence. Although initially appearing as a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) attack under the Chaos brand, evidence suggests it was a targeted state-backed attack. The attackers used interactive screen-sharing to harvest credentials and manipulate multi-factor authentication (MFA). Once inside, they bypassed traditional ransomware workflows, opting for data exfiltration and long-term persistence using tools like DWAgent. MuddyWater's use of off-the-shelf tools like CastleRAT and Tsundere has been documented by multiple cybersecurity firms. The attack highlights the convergence of state-sponsored intrusion activity and cybercriminal tradecraft to obscure attribution and delay defensive responses.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance via social engineering on Microsoft Teams. The attack's sophistication and strategic objectives underscore the need for robust detection and remediation strategies.

doc_summary: A critical vulnerability identified in Argo CD, tracked as CVE-2026-42880, allows attackers with minimal privileges to extract sensitive Kubernetes Secrets from etcd clusters. Rated 9.6, this flaw involves a missing authorization and data-masking gap in the ServerSideDiff endpoint. The vulnerability affects Argo CD versions 3.2.0 to 3.3.8 and is exploited when the compare-options annotation with mutation webhooks is enabled. A proof-of-concept Python script demonstrates the extraction process using the grpc-web protocol. The flaw poses a significant threat to cloud-native environments, allowing attackers to access service account tokens, database credentials, API keys, and TLS certificates. Security researcher Hoang-Prod reported the issue, and patched versions 3.3.9 and 3.2.11 have been released to address the vulnerability.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server, specifically a double-free issue in the HTTP/2 protocol handling. The attack surface is significant due to the widespread use of HTTP/2 in production environments.
doc_summary: The Apache Software Foundation released security updates for the Apache HTTP Server to address vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-23918, a critical double-free vulnerability in the HTTP/2 protocol handling. This vulnerability, discovered by Bartlomiej Dmitruk of Striga.ai and Stanislaw Strzalkowski of ISEC.pl, affects Apache HTTP Server 2.4.66 and allows for denial-of-service (DoS) and remote code execution (RCE). The issue arises when a client sends an HTTP/2 HEADERS frame followed by RST_STREAM with a non-zero error code, leading to memory being freed twice. The RCE path requires an Apache Portable Runtime with the mmap allocator, common on Debian systems. The vulnerability is critical due to its potential impact on widely deployed systems. Users are advised to update to version 2.4.67 for protection.

doc_summary: A sophisticated China-nexus advanced persistent threat (APT) group, UAT-8302, has been attributed to attacks targeting government entities in South America since late 2024 and government agencies in southeastern Europe in 2025. The group uses custom-made malware families, including a .NET-based backdoor dubbed NetDraft (aka NosyDoor), a C# variant of FINALDRAFT (aka Squidoor). ESET tracks the use of NosyDoor to a group called LongNosedGoblin. The same malware has been deployed against Russian IT organizations by a threat actor referred to as Erudite Mogwai (aka Space Pirates and Webworm). UAT-8302 uses tools like SNOWRUST to download the VShell payload and sets up alternative backdoor access using proxy and VPN tools like Stowaway and SoftEther VPN. The group is suspected of using zero-day and N-day exploits in web applications for initial access. Trend Micro highlights a phenomenon called Premier Pass-as-a-Service, where initial access obtained by Earth Estries is passed to Earth Naga for follow-on exploitation.
kill_chain_summary: The UAT-8302 APT group's attack chain involves reconnaissance using open-source tools, weaponization through custom malware development, and delivery via zero-day exploits in web applications. Title: CloudZ RAT Deploys Pheno Plugin to Hijack Microsoft Phone Link

Victim.Description: Victims are users of Windows 10 and 11 with Microsoft Phone Link installed.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the deployment of CloudZ RAT with the Pheno plugin, targeting Microsoft Phone Link to intercept SMS and OTPs. The adversary's capability includes using a Rust-based loader and a .NET loader for installation, with persistence achieved via scheduled tasks. The infrastructure involves HTTP traffic with anti-caching headers. Victims are users of Windows 10 and 11 with Microsoft Phone Link installed.
doc_summary: CloudZ RAT, a remote access tool, has been updated with a new plugin called Pheno, which hijacks the Microsoft Phone Link application to steal sensitive codes from mobile devices. The malware was active since January and aims to steal credentials and temporary passcodes. Microsoft Phone Link, pre-installed on Windows 10 and 11, allows users to manage calls, texts, and notifications from their mobile devices. The Pheno plugin monitors active Phone Link sessions and accesses its local SQLite database, potentially compromising SMS and OTP messages. Cisco Talos researchers discovered that CloudZ RAT rotates between three hardcoded user-agent strings to disguise its HTTP traffic. The initial access vector is unknown, but the infection begins with a fake ScreenConnect update, deploying a Rust-based loader followed by a .NET loader, which installs CloudZ RAT and establishes persistence via a scheduled task. The .NET loader includes anti-analysis checks. Users are advised to avoid SMS-based OTP services and use phishing-resistant solutions like hardware keys. Cisco Talos has published indicators of compromise, including URLs, hashes, domains, and IP addresses.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with a fake ScreenConnect update, leading to the installation of CloudZ RAT via a Rust-based loader and a .NET loader. Persistence is established through scheduled tasks. The Pheno plugin intercepts SMS and OTPs by accessing the SQLite database of Microsoft Phone Link. Command and control are maintained through HTTP traffic with anti-caching headers.

Title: Sentencing of Deniss Zolotarjovs for Karakurt Ransomware Activities

diamond_model_summary: Deniss Zolotarjovs, a member of the Karakurt ransomware group, played a crucial role in extortion activities targeting American organizations. His involvement included negotiating ransom payments and using stolen information to apply psychological pressure on victims. The Karakurt group, associated with former Conti leaders, caused significant financial losses.
doc_summary: Deniss Zolotarjovs, a Latvian national, was extradited to the United States and sentenced to 8.5 years in prison for his role in the Karakurt ransomware group. Zolotarjovs, also known as Sforza_cesarini, was involved in extortion activities targeting American organizations, including a government entity. He was linked to at least six extortion cases between August 2021 and November 2023. The Karakurt group, led by former Conti ransomware leaders, compromised systems, stole data, and demanded ransom. Zolotarjovs used stolen children's health information to increase leverage in extortion. The Department of Justice reported over $56 million in losses from 13 companies, with additional ransom payments from 41 companies. The true loss numbers are uncertain due to underreporting. Zolotarjovs is the first Karakurt member sentenced in the US, potentially leading to further prosecutions.
kill_chain_summary: The Karakurt ransomware group's activities involved reconnaissance to gather victim information, followed by actions on objectives where stolen data was used to coerce victims into paying ransoms. Deniss Zolotarjovs was instrumental in negotiating these extortions, leveraging stolen personal and health information to increase pressure on victims.

doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-22679, in Weaver E-cology, an enterprise office automation platform, has been actively exploited. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution via the '/papi/esearch/data/devops/dubboApi/debug/method' endpoint. The Shadowserver Foundation observed exploitation starting March 31, 2026, while QiAnXin reproduced the vulnerability on March 17, 2026. The Vega Research Team reported exploitation evidence from March 17, 2026. Attackers used POST requests with controlled parameters to execute arbitrary commands. The campaign involved RCE verification, failed payload drops, and attempts to retrieve PowerShell payloads. A Python detection script is available to identify vulnerable instances. Users are advised to apply patches to mitigate the risk.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with exploitation of CVE-2026-22679, allowing remote code execution on Weaver E-cology systems. The adversary attempts to install MSI payloads and retrieve PowerShell scripts for persistence. Discovery commands are executed to gather system information. The attack highlights the importance of timely patching and monitoring for unusual activity.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the vulnerability CVE-2026-22679 as a TTP, and the MSI filename 'fanwei0324.msi' as a network host artifact. doc_summary: ScarCruft, a North Korea-aligned state-sponsored hacking group, has compromised the sqgame.net gaming platform in a supply chain attack, deploying the BirdCall backdoor. The attack highlights ScarCruft's focus on North Korean defectors and human rights activists. The Android variant collects personal data, while the Windows version includes a downloader for RokRAT. The vulnerability affects Android versions 14, 15, 16, and 16-qpr2. Google can push fixes through Google Play system updates, enabling faster remediation. Users must update to the 2026-05-01 security patch level to mitigate risks. The attack vector is proximal or adjacent, making public Wi-Fi networks potential targets. Organizations should prioritize deploying updates to secure mobile fleets.

diamond_model_summary: The VENOMOUS#HELPER campaign is characterized by the use of legitimate RMM tools like SimpleHelp and ScreenConnect to establish persistent access to victim systems. The adversary, likely a financially motivated Initial Access Broker or ransomware precursor, targets organizations primarily in the United States. The infrastructure involves compromised domains and legitimate software for command and control. The campaign's strategic objective is to maintain persistent access for financial gain.
doc_summary: An active phishing campaign, codenamed VENOMOUS#HELPER, has been targeting multiple vectors since April 2025, using legitimate Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) software like SimpleHelp and ScreenConnect to establish persistent remote access. The campaign has impacted over 80 organizations, primarily in the United States, and is believed to be linked to a financially motivated Initial Access Broker or ransomware precursor operation. The attack begins with phishing emails impersonating the US Social Security Administration, directing victims to download a malicious executable from a compromised Mexican business website. The malware installs as a Windows service with Safe Mode persistence and uses a self-healing watchdog to maintain its presence. It also enumerates security products and polls user presence. The SimpleHelp client acquires SeDebugPrivilege for elevated access, allowing the attacker to execute commands, transfer files, and pivot to adjacent systems. The campaign uses a redundant dual-channel access architecture to evade detection.
kill_chain_summary: The VENOMOUS#HELPER campaign follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify targets, followed by weaponization through phishing emails impersonating the US Social Security Administration. Delivery occurs via emails directing victims to download a malicious executable. Exploitation involves user execution of the file, leading to installation as a Windows service with persistence mechanisms. Command and control is maintained through SimpleHelp and ScreenConnect, allowing the adversary to execute commands and transfer files. Actions on objectives include data collection and lateral movement.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The VENOMOUS#HELPER campaign presents challenges at various levels of the Pyramid of Pain. The use of legitimate RMM tools like SimpleHelp and ScreenConnect complicates detection and response efforts. The campaign's reliance on compromised domains and legitimate software for command and control further complicates attribution and mitigation. The adversary's tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) include phishing, use of legitimate software, and redundant dual-channel access, making it difficult to disrupt their operations.

Victim.Description: Users of the PyTorch Lightning package version 2.6.3

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a supply chain attack on the PyTorch Lightning package, where a malicious version was published on PyPI. doc_summary: A supply chain attack was disclosed on April 30, 2023, involving a malicious version of the PyTorch Lightning package on PyPI. The compromised version 2.6.3 included a hidden execution chain that downloaded and executed a heavily obfuscated JavaScript payload, identified as ShaiWorm, targeting credentials in browsers, environment files, and cloud services like AWS, Azure, and GCP. Microsoft Threat Intelligence detected and prevented the attack, which affected a small number of devices. The package was reverted to a safe version 2.6.1. The attack highlights risks in software supply chains and the need for immediate rotation of compromised secrets.

Victim.Description: Victims are users of cPanel and WHM who have not patched the critical vulnerability CVE-2026-41940.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a sophisticated adversary exploiting a critical vulnerability in cPanel and WHM, tracked as CVE-2026-41940. The adversary's capability includes deploying Mirai botnet variants and Sorry ransomware, indicating a high level of sophistication. The infrastructure used involves compromised web hosting environments, and the victims are primarily users of cPanel and WHM who have not patched the vulnerability. The adversary's motivation appears to be financial gain through ransomware deployment and botnet control.
doc_summary: This report analyzes the active exploitation of a critical vulnerability in cPanel and WebHost Manager (WHM), tracked as CVE-2026-41940. The flaw allows for authentication bypass, enabling remote attackers to gain elevated control over the control panel. This has led to severe consequences, including the complete wipe of websites and backups, as well as the deployment of Mirai botnet variants and a ransomware strain called Sorry. The incident highlights the increasing professionalism of underground cybercriminals, who are leveraging trusted commits and scaling operations akin to legitimate businesses. The report emphasizes the urgency of patching vulnerabilities, particularly those marked as critical, to mitigate the risk of exploitation. The text also references other high-severity vulnerabilities, such as CVE-2026-31431 in the Linux Kernel and CVE-2026-42208 in LiteLLM, underscoring the shrinking gap between patch releases and exploitations. Organizations are advised to verify supply chains, tighten SaaS access, and treat routine logins as potentially hostile to prevent further breaches.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves multiple stages, starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable cPanel and WHM instances. The adversary then weaponized the vulnerability CVE-2026-41940 to bypass authentication and gain initial access. Delivery of the exploit was achieved via remote access to vulnerable systems, followed by exploitation to gain control over cPanel and WHM. Installation of Mirai botnet and Sorry ransomware was conducted on compromised systems, establishing command and control. Finally, the adversary executed actions on objectives by deploying ransomware and wiping websites and backups.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes several indicators of compromise. Hash values for the Mirai botnet and Sorry ransomware are critical for detection. IP addresses and domain names associated with command and control servers are also significant indicators. Network host artifacts related to the exploitation of cPanel and WHM provide additional detection opportunities. Tools used by the adversary include the Mirai botnet and Sorry ransomware, while TTPs involve authentication bypass and ransomware deployment.

Title: Silver Fox Cyber Attack Campaign Targeting Russia and India with ABCDoor Malware

Victim.Description: Organizations in Russia and India across industrial, consulting, retail, and transportation sectors.

diamond_model_summary: The Silver Fox cybercrime group, based in China, has been linked to a sophisticated campaign targeting organizations in Russia and India. The group employs phishing emails mimicking official tax notices to deliver malware such as ValleyRAT and ABCDoor. Their infrastructure includes domains like abc.haijing88.com, and they target sectors like industrial, consulting, retail, and transportation. Silver Fox's strategic objectives include espionage and financial gain, using advanced techniques like Phantom Persistence and geofencing.
doc_summary: The China-based cybercrime group Silver Fox has launched a new campaign targeting organizations in Russia and India using the ABCDoor malware. The attack involved phishing emails mimicking the Income Tax Department of India, leading to the download of a Rust-based loader and the ValleyRAT backdoor. The campaign impacted sectors such as industrial, consulting, retail, and transportation, with over 1,600 phishing emails flagged. The attack chain starts with a phishing email containing a PDF file with links to download a ZIP or RAR archive from abc.haijing88.com. The archive contains a modified RustSL loader that unpacks the encrypted payload, implementing geofencing and environment checks. The loader employs Phantom Persistence to establish persistence. The encrypted payload downloads the ValleyRAT malware, which facilitates command-and-control communications and additional module execution. The ABCDoor backdoor enables data collection, remote control, and exfiltration. Silver Fox has expanded its geographic focus to include Japan, with the highest number of attacks detected in India, Russia, and Indonesia.
kill_chain_summary: The Silver Fox campaign follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify targets, followed by weaponization of phishing emails with malicious attachments. Delivery occurs through phishing emails, leading to exploitation when users interact with the attachments. Installation involves the RustSL loader, which unpacks the payload. Command and control is established via ValleyRAT, and actions on objectives include data collection and exfiltration using the ABCDoor backdoor. The campaign demonstrates advanced tactics and techniques across the kill chain.

Title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in FreeBSD DHCP Client (CVE-2026-42511)

Victim.Description: FreeBSD systems using dhclient for network configuration

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical RCE vulnerability in FreeBSD's DHCP client, allowing local network attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges. The adversary exploits the dhclient utility's improper handling of DHCP lease options, injecting malicious directives into the dhclient.conf file. The infrastructure includes a rogue DHCP server on the local network, targeting FreeBSD systems using dhclient for network configuration. The attack results in complete system compromise, with the potential for persistence and lateral movement.
doc_summary: The FreeBSD Project has issued a critical security advisory (FreeBSD-SA-26:12.dhclient) addressing a severe Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in its default IPv4 DHCP client, tracked as CVE-2026-42511. Discovered by Joshua Rogers of the AISLE Research Team, this flaw allows local network attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges. The vulnerability affects all supported versions of FreeBSD and originates from how the dhclient(8) utility handles malicious DHCP lease options. Specifically, the flaw is triggered when the BOOTP file field is written to the system’s lease file without properly escaping embedded double-quotes, allowing threat actors to inject arbitrary directives into the dhclient.conf file. The malicious payload remains dormant until the DHCP lease file is re-parsed, typically during a system restart or network interface initialization. Successful exploitation requires the attacker to be on the same local broadcast domain as the target, deploying a rogue DHCP server to intercept legitimate DHCP requests and reply with a maliciously crafted BOOTP file field. This attack vector results in complete system compromise, with the injected code executing with root permissions, enabling the installation of persistence mechanisms, malware deployment, or lateral movement within the compromised network. Affected versions include FreeBSD 15, 14, and 13. Administrators are urged to apply the latest security patches immediately and consider implementing network-level defenses such as DHCP snooping to block rogue DHCP servers.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable FreeBSD systems on the local network. Weaponization involves crafting a malicious DHCP response, followed by delivery through a rogue DHCP server. Exploitation occurs when the payload is executed via dhclient re-parsing. Installation involves persistence mechanisms using root access. Actions on objectives include performing tasks with root privileges. doc_summary: Microsoft Defender mistakenly flagged legitimate DigiCert root certificates as Trojan:Win32/Cerdigent.A!dha, causing false-positive alerts and certificate removal from Windows systems. This issue arose after a Defender signature update on April 30th. DigiCert experienced a breach where attackers obtained initialization codes for code-signing certificates, leading to their misuse in malware campaigns. DigiCert revoked 60 certificates, including 27 linked to malware. The breach involved a compromised support staff member and exposed initialization codes for EV code-signing certificates. Microsoft released a fix in Security Intelligence update 1.449.431.0, restoring removed certificates. The incident is linked to the GoldenEyeDog group, using DigiCert certificates to sign malware like Zhong Stealer.
kill_chain_summary: The adversary conducted reconnaissance to identify vulnerabilities in DigiCert's support environment, weaponized phishing emails with malicious attachments, and delivered them to DigiCert's support staff. doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added a security flaw impacting Linux distributions to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-31431, is a local privilege escalation flaw allowing unprivileged users to gain root access. Known as Copy Fail, it results from a logic bug in the Linux kernel's authentication cryptographic template. The flaw affects Linux distributions since 2017 and poses risks to containerized environments. Exploitation is facilitated by a 732-byte Python-based exploit, with Go and Rust versions detected. The vulnerability is not remotely exploitable but becomes impactful when combined with initial access vectors like SSH. CISA advises applying fixes by May 15, 2026, or implementing mitigations like disabling the affected feature and network isolation.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves weaponization of the CVE-2026-31431 vulnerability through a Python-based exploit, leading to local privilege escalation in Linux systems. The exploitation stage is critical, allowing attackers to gain root access by corrupting the kernel's in-memory page cache. The vulnerability is not remotely exploitable but becomes impactful when combined with initial access vectors like SSH. The actions on objectives stage involves breaching container isolation and gaining control over the physical machine. Detection is challenging due to the use of legitimate system calls.

Title: SHADOW-EARTH-053 Espionage Campaign Targeting Asia and Europe

Victim.Description: Government and defense sectors in Asia and Europe.
Victim.Geography: South, East, Southeast Asia, and Poland

diamond_model_summary: The SHADOW-EARTH-053 campaign is a sophisticated espionage operation attributed to China-aligned threat actors. It targets government and defense sectors in Asia and Europe, exploiting vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange and IIS servers. The adversary employs advanced techniques such as DLL sideloading and web shells for persistence, with ShadowPad and Noodle RAT as primary malware. The infrastructure includes compromised servers and open-source tunneling tools, while victims are primarily in Pakistan, Thailand, Malaysia, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, and Poland. The campaign's strategic objective is intelligence gathering, with a high level of sophistication and motivation for espionage.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers disclosed a China-aligned espionage campaign, SHADOW-EARTH-053, targeting government and defense sectors in South, East, and Southeast Asia, and Poland. Trend Micro attributed the activity to SHADOW-EARTH-053, active since December 2024, with network overlap with CL-STA-0049, Earth Alux, and REF7707. The group exploits N-day vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange and IIS servers, deploying Godzilla web shells for persistent access and ShadowPad implants via DLL sideloading. Targets include Pakistan, Thailand, Malaysia, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, and Poland. Nearly half the targets were also compromised by SHADOW-EARTH-054. The attacks start with exploiting known security flaws, dropping web shells like Godzilla, and deploying ShadowPad via AnyDesk. React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) facilitated Noodle RAT distribution. Open-source tunneling tools like IOX, GOST, and Wstunnel, and RingQ for packing binaries were used. Mimikatz and Sharp-SMBExec were used for privilege escalation and lateral movement. The primary entry vector was vulnerabilities in IIS applications. Citizen Lab flagged phishing campaigns by GLITTER CARP and SEQUIN CARP targeting journalists and civil society, linked to Chinese intelligence priorities.
kill_chain_summary: The SHADOW-EARTH-053 campaign follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the exploitation of vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange and IIS servers for initial access. Web shells like Godzilla are deployed for persistence, followed by the installation of ShadowPad implants via DLL sideloading. Command and control is maintained through AnyDesk and tunneling tools, enabling data exfiltration and further reconnaissance. The campaign employs advanced tactics for privilege escalation and lateral movement, using tools like Mimikatz and Sharp-SMBExec. The primary objective is to gather intelligence from government and defense sectors, with a high impact severity due to the critical nature of the targeted assets.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The SHADOW-EARTH-053 campaign presents significant challenges across the Pyramid of Pain. The use of specific malware families like ShadowPad and Noodle RAT, along with tools such as Mimikatz and Sharp-SMBExec, increases the difficulty of detection and response. The exploitation of known vulnerabilities and deployment of web shells complicates defensive measures. The campaign's infrastructure, including compromised servers and tunneling tools, adds layers of complexity. The adversary's tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) demonstrate a high level of sophistication, making it challenging to disrupt their operations effectively.

Title: Supply Chain Attack via Malicious Ruby Gems and Go Modules

Victim.Description: The victims are developers and CI environments using Ruby and Go ecosystems.

diamond_model_summary: The attack involves the adversary BufferZoneCorp using malicious Ruby gems and Go modules to target software development environments. The capability includes credential theft and GitHub Actions tampering, with infrastructure involving GitHub repositories and Webhook.site for data exfiltration. Victims are developers and CI environments, with high impact severity.
doc_summary: A new software supply chain attack campaign has been observed using sleeper packages to push malicious payloads enabling credential theft, GitHub Actions tampering, and SSH persistence. The activity is attributed to the GitHub account BufferZoneCorp, which published repositories associated with malicious Ruby gems and Go modules. The packages, masquerading as well-known modules like activesupport-logger and devise-jwt, were yanked from RubyGems and blocked in Go. The Ruby gems automate credential theft during install, exfiltrating data to a Webhook.site endpoint. The Go modules tamper with GitHub Actions workflows, plant fake Go wrappers, and add SSH keys for remote access. Users are advised to remove the packages, review for unauthorized changes, rotate credentials, and inspect network logs for exfiltration traffic.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain: weaponization through malicious package creation, delivery via RubyGems and Go repositories, exploitation of developer environments, installation of payloads, command and control through data exfiltration to Webhook.site, and actions on objectives involving credential theft and SSH persistence.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like webhook.site, tools such as malicious Ruby gems and Go modules, and TTPs involving credential theft and GitHub Actions tampering. These indicators are crucial for detection and response efforts, with a focus on identifying and mitigating the use of compromised packages.

doc_summary: The Exim mail server developers released version 4.99.2 to address four critical security vulnerabilities identified as CVE-2026-40684, CVE-2026-40685, CVE-2026-40686, and CVE-2026-40687. These vulnerabilities could lead to denial-of-service attacks, memory heap corruption, and potential data leaks. The update was shared with Linux distribution maintainers on April 24, 2026, and publicly released on April 29, 2026. Exim, a popular message transfer agent for Unix-like systems, requires timely patching to prevent exploitation by malicious actors. The vulnerabilities involve issues with DNS data, JSON data processing, UTF-8 character handling, and SPA authentication. Administrators are urged to upgrade to the latest version to secure their email infrastructure.

Title: Cyber-Enabled Cargo Theft in Transportation and Logistics Industry

Victim.Description: Transportation and logistics companies in the United States and Canada.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable to phishing and impersonation attacks
Targeted_Assets: Computer systems of freight brokers and carriers

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors, identified as the Diesel Vortex group, targeting the transportation and logistics industry in the United States and Canada. They employ sophisticated phishing and impersonation tactics to infiltrate systems, post fraudulent listings, and reroute high-value freight. The adversaries demonstrate high sophistication and financial motivation, leveraging compromised infrastructure to achieve their objectives.
doc_summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has issued a warning to the transportation and logistics industry about a significant increase in cyber-enabled cargo theft. Estimated losses in the United States and Canada are projected to reach nearly $725 million by 2025, marking a 60% increase from the previous year. Criminals are employing hacking and impersonation tactics to hijack high-value freight. Confirmed cargo theft incidents rose by 18% last year, with the average value per theft increasing by 36% to $273,990. Threat actors are infiltrating computer systems of freight brokers and carriers using spoofed emails and fake web links. Once inside, they post fraudulent listings on online load boards and impersonate legitimate companies to divert shipments. The Diesel Vortex threat group has been identified in phishing attacks since September 2025, using 52 domains. The FBI advises companies to verify shipment requests through secondary channels, implement multi-factor authentication, and maintain detailed records of vehicles and drivers. Victims are encouraged to file complaints with the Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to gather information on targets. Weaponization involves creating spoofed emails and fake web links. Delivery is executed through phishing emails, leading to exploitation via credential access. Installation of remote monitoring software enables persistence, while command and control is established through compromised systems. Actions on objectives include posting fraudulent listings and rerouting shipments.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names used in phishing attacks, which are moderately difficult for adversaries to change. The use of spoofed emails and fake web links represents a significant challenge for defenders to detect and block. The adversaries' tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) are well-developed, indicating a high level of sophistication and persistence in achieving their objectives.

doc_summary: Thomasz Szabo, a Romanian national, led an online swatting ring targeting over 75 public officials, journalists, and religious institutions. doc_summary: In April 2026, a supply chain attack compromised the Python package 'Lightning', leading to credential theft. The attack involved malicious versions 2.6.2 and 2.6.3, published on April 30, 2026. The campaign is linked to the Mini Shai-Hulud incident targeting SAP-related npm packages. The attack is attributed to TeamPCP, with connections to LAPSUS$. The PyPI repository quarantined the project, and developers are advised to block and remove affected versions, downgrading to version 2.6.1. The incident highlights vulnerabilities in open-source software supply chains.

doc_summary: A joint international operation led by Dubai Police and involving U.S. and Chinese authorities resulted in the arrest of 276 suspects and the shutdown of nine cryptocurrency investment fraud centers. The operation targeted crime networks running pig-butchering schemes, a form of fraud where scammers build trust with victims through fake friendships or romances before luring them to fraudulent cryptocurrency investment platforms. Victims lost control of their funds, which were laundered through additional cryptocurrency accounts. Key figures arrested include Burmese national Thet Min Nyi and Indonesian nationals Wiliang Awang, Andreas Chandra, and Lisa Mariam. The operation highlights the borderless nature of fraud and the global efforts to combat it. The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center identified numerous victims across the United States, with investment fraud accounting for significant financial losses.

Title: Copy Fail: Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability in Linux Kernels

Victim.Description: Linux distributions running kernels released since 2017 are affected.

diamond_model_summary: The 'Copy Fail' vulnerability represents a significant threat to Linux systems, allowing local privilege escalation through a logic bug in the authencesn cryptographic template. Theori's development of a Python-based exploit demonstrates the capability to exploit this flaw across multiple Linux distributions. The vulnerability affects systems globally, with a high impact severity due to the potential for root access.
doc_summary: An exploit named 'Copy Fail' targets a local privilege escalation vulnerability in Linux kernels since 2017, tracked as CVE-2026-31431. Discovered by Theori using its AI-driven platform Xint Code, the flaw allows unprivileged users to gain root access by exploiting a logic bug in the authencesn cryptographic template. The vulnerability involves a 4-byte write into the page cache of any readable file, potentially altering setuid-root binaries. Theori's proof-of-concept exploit affects major Linux distributions like Ubuntu, Amazon Linux, RHEL, and SUSE. The flaw was introduced with an 'in-place' optimization in 2017 and fixed by reverting this behavior. Patches are available, but some distributions lack official updates. Interim mitigations include disabling the vulnerable crypto interface.
kill_chain_summary: The 'Copy Fail' vulnerability follows a clear kill chain, beginning with the discovery and weaponization of the exploit by Theori. The exploitation stage is critical, as it allows unprivileged users to gain root access by altering setuid-root binaries. The lack of significant activity in other stages highlights the exploit's focus on privilege escalation. Remediation efforts include patching and disabling the vulnerable crypto interface.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The 'Copy Fail' vulnerability primarily involves a specific exploit (CVE-2026-31431) and a Python-based tool developed by Theori. The lack of specific indicators such as IP addresses or domain names limits the Pyramid of Pain's applicability. However, the exploit's broad applicability across Linux distributions increases its impact, emphasizing the need for timely patching and mitigation strategies.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a stealthy Python-based backdoor framework called DEEP#DOOR. Title: Critical OS Command Injection Vulnerability in ASUSTOR ADM

Victim.Description: ASUSTOR NAS devices vulnerable to command injection.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to default credentials and unpatched firmware.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in ASUSTOR's ADM operating system, specifically within the PPTP VPN Client feature. The vulnerability allows authenticated administrators to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges due to improper input sanitization. The adversary could exploit default credentials to gain access, highlighting the importance of changing default passwords and applying patches. The infrastructure at risk includes ASUSTOR NAS devices, with a potential exposure of approximately 19,000 internet-facing hosts. The victim profile is broad, affecting any organization using vulnerable ASUSTOR devices.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-6644, was discovered in ASUSTOR's ADM operating system, specifically in the PPTP VPN Client feature. This OS command injection vulnerability, with a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.4, allows an authenticated administrator to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges. The flaw is located in the PPTP VPN connection handler at /portal/apis/settings/vpn.cgi, where the server address input is not properly sanitized. ASUSTOR has addressed the issue in ADM version 5.1.3.RGO1. The vulnerability is not pre-authentication; attackers must gain administrator access, which is facilitated by default credentials (admin/admin). Once root access is achieved, attackers can install malware, access data, or use the device for DDoS attacks. Approximately 19,000 internet-facing ASUSTOR hosts are potential targets. Security measures include updating firmware, changing default credentials, and restricting management interface access.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where threat actors may scan for vulnerable ASUSTOR NAS devices. Weaponization involves the development of a Python-based PoC script to exploit the command injection vulnerability. Exploitation occurs when the attacker uses the script to gain root access. Installation may involve deploying persistent malware on compromised devices. Actions on objectives include data theft or using the device for DDoS attacks. The incident highlights the need for immediate remediation, including firmware updates and changing default credentials.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes a Python-based PoC script as a tool, and the TTPs involve command injection and exploitation of default credentials. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified, limiting the ability to track the adversary through traditional indicators. The focus should be on detecting behavioral patterns and applying patches to mitigate the vulnerability. The incident underscores the importance of securing default credentials and monitoring for unusual command execution patterns.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a high-severity Linux local privilege escalation vulnerability, CVE-2026-31431, codenamed 'Copy Fail'. This flaw allows an unprivileged local user to gain root access by writing controlled bytes into the page cache of any readable file. The vulnerability, introduced in a 2017 source code commit, affects all Linux distributions since 2017, including Amazon Linux, RHEL, SUSE, and Ubuntu. The issue lies in the Linux kernel's cryptographic subsystem, specifically the algif_aead module. Exploitation involves a 732-byte Python script that edits a setuid binary. The vulnerability is similar to the Dirty Pipe (CVE-2022-0847) vulnerability. It is dangerous due to its portability, stealth, and cross-container impact, allowing privilege escalation and sandbox bypassing.

The vulnerability's cross-container impact increases its severity.

Title: Jenkins Security Advisory: Multiple Plugin Vulnerabilities

Victim.Description: Organizations using Jenkins CI/CD pipelines with vulnerable plugins.

diamond_model_summary: The Jenkins security advisory highlights vulnerabilities in multiple plugins, posing a high risk to CI/CD environments. The most severe issue, CVE-2026-42520, involves a path traversal flaw in the Credentials Binding Plugin, potentially leading to remote code execution. Other vulnerabilities include stored XSS in the GitHub and HTML Publisher plugins. Administrators are urged to update affected components immediately to mitigate risks.
doc_summary: The Jenkins project released a critical security advisory addressing seven vulnerabilities across multiple widely used plugins. The disclosed flaws include high-severity path traversal and stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities that could allow threat actors to execute arbitrary code or hijack user sessions. All vulnerabilities were responsibly disclosed through the Jenkins Bug Bounty Program, which the European Commission sponsors. System administrators are strongly advised to update their environments immediately to prevent exploitation in their continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines. The most severe vulnerability addressed in this advisory is a high-severity path traversal flaw tracked as CVE-2026-42520. This issue impacts the Credentials Binding Plugin up to version 719.v80e905ef14eb_. The plugin previously failed to sanitize file names for file and zip file credentials. This oversight allows attackers who can provide credentials to a job to write files to arbitrary locations on the node’s filesystem. If a Jenkins environment is configured to allow a low-privileged user to configure file credentials for a job running on the built-in node, this path traversal can easily escalate to remote code execution (RCE). The vulnerability is patched in version 720.v3f6decef43ea_ by enforcing proper file name sanitization. The advisory also highlights two high-severity stored XSS vulnerabilities impacting popular plugins. GitHub Plugin (CVE-2026-42523): Versions 1.46.0 and earlier improperly process the current job URL during JavaScript validation for the “GitHub hook trigger for GITScm polling” feature. Non-anonymous attackers possessing Overall/Read permissions can exploit this flaw to inject malicious scripts. It is resolved in version 1.46.0.1. HTML Publisher Plugin (CVE-2026-42524): Versions 427 and earlier fail to safely escape the job name and URL within legacy wrapper files. Attackers with Item/Configure permission can exploit this to launch stored XSS attacks. Version 427.1 corrects this behavior for newly generated wrappers, and environments strictly enforcing Content Security Policy (CSP) protections are inherently mitigated against this flaw. Additionally, the update addresses four medium-severity flaws that could facilitate information disclosure or phishing campaigns: Script Security Plugin (CVE-2026-42519): A missing permission check in an HTTP endpoint allows attackers with Overall/Read permission to enumerate pending and approved classpaths improperly. Matrix Authorization Strategy Plugin (CVE-2026-42521): An unsafe deserialization bug allows attackers with Item/Configure permission to instantiate arbitrary types by invoking parameterless constructors, potentially leading to unauthorized information disclosure. GitHub Branch Source Plugin (CVE-2026-42522): A missing permission check enables attackers to perform unauthorized connection tests using attacker-specified GitHub App credentials. Microsoft Entra ID Plugin (CVE-2026-42525): An open redirect vulnerability allows attackers to conduct phishing attacks by redirecting users to malicious external sites immediately following successful authentication.
kill_chain_summary: The Jenkins vulnerabilities primarily affect the Exploitation and Actions on Objectives stages of the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain. Exploitation involves leveraging plugin vulnerabilities for arbitrary code execution and XSS attacks. Actions on Objectives may include remote code execution and session hijacking. Immediate patching and strict permission controls are recommended to prevent exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes vulnerabilities (TTPs) such as CVE-2026-42520, CVE-2026-42523, and CVE-2026-42524. These vulnerabilities allow for path traversal and XSS attacks, posing significant challenges to defenders. Effective detection and remediation require monitoring Jenkins logs and applying patches to vulnerable plugins.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-41940, exploited by adversaries to gain unauthorized access to cPanel and WHM servers. The infrastructure targeted is primarily within the web hosting industry, affecting global hosting providers. Victims are web hosting providers using cPanel and WHM, with a high impact severity due to potential data breaches and system takeovers.
doc_summary: A critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-41940, is actively exploited in the web hosting industry. This CVSS 9.8 flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass cPanel and WHM login mechanisms, granting full administrative control over servers. The vulnerability stems from a CRLF injection flaw in the session loading and saving process. Attackers inject a malicious security token into a pre-authenticated session, bypassing password validation checks. Security firm watchTowr Labs published a PoC exploit script achieving Remote Code Execution. Global hosting providers block control panel ports to protect data. Exploited servers can be manipulated for ransomware deployment, data exfiltration, or downstream attacks. Even outdated cPanel versions are vulnerable. Administrators must update to secure releases and investigate session logs for multi-line password values or unexpected token_denied entries. Organizations should purge active sessions, reset root passwords, and audit systems for persistence mechanisms. Firewalls should block inbound traffic on TCP ports 2083, 2087, 2095, and 2096. cPanel's detection script can scan for compromise indicators.

doc_summary: Google has addressed a critical security flaw in the Gemini CLI npm package and GitHub Actions workflow, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands on host systems. It allowed unprivileged attackers to load malicious content as Gemini configuration, leading to command execution on the host system. The flaw does not have a CVE identifier. doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in ProFTPD's mod_sql extension, tracked as CVE-2026-42167, allows attackers to exploit SQL injection to achieve authentication bypass, privilege escalation, and potentially remote code execution. Discovered by ZeroPath Research, this flaw affects ProFTPD versions up to 1.3.9 and is particularly dangerous for internet-facing FTP servers using SQL-backed logging or authentication. The vulnerability arises from improper handling of attacker-controlled data, such as usernames, in SQL queries. If mod_sql logging is enabled for pre-authentication commands, a remote attacker can exploit the flaw without valid login credentials. The risk is heightened when ProFTPD is connected to PostgreSQL with high privileges, enabling SQL injection to lead to operating system command execution. Administrators are urged to upgrade to ProFTPD 1.3.9a, review mod_sql configurations, and monitor for unusual activity. The CVE has a CVSS v3 score of 8.1, indicating high severity.
kill_chain_summary: The ProFTPD vulnerability CVE-2026-42167 follows a kill chain that begins with exploiting a SQL injection flaw in the mod_sql extension. This allows adversaries to gain initial access without valid credentials, leading to potential privilege escalation and remote code execution. The exploitation stage is critical, as it enables attackers to manipulate SQL queries and execute arbitrary commands. diamond_model_summary: The attack on SAP npm packages is attributed to TeamPCP, who used a supply-chain attack to compromise enterprise development environments. doc_summary: The incident involves a supply-chain attack by TeamPCP on multiple official SAP npm packages, impacting SAP's Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP) and Cloud MTA. The attack included a malicious 'preinstall' script that executed a loader named setup.mjs, downloading the Bun JavaScript runtime from GitHub to execute an obfuscated execution.js payload. This payload acted as an information-stealer, targeting credentials from developer machines and CI/CD environments. The malware extracted secrets from CI runner memory and uploaded encrypted data to public GitHub repositories. The attack used GitHub commit searches as a dead-drop mechanism for tokens, allowing further access and propagation to other packages. The attack is linked to TeamPCP, known for similar tactics in previous supply-chain attacks against Trivy, Checkmarx, and Bitwarden. The compromise may have involved an exposed NPM token via a misconfigured CircleCI job.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, starting with the weaponization of npm packages by adding a malicious 'preinstall' script. The script was delivered via npm package installation, executing an information-stealer payload. The payload installed and executed on victim systems, using GitHub as a command and control channel. The malware collected credentials and attempted to propagate to other packages, demonstrating a sophisticated supply-chain attack by TeamPCP.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like github.com, tools such as the Bun JavaScript runtime, and TTPs like supply-chain compromise and credential theft. The adversary's use of GitHub as a dead-drop mechanism and obfuscated JavaScript payloads are key indicators. The attack's complexity and use of widely trusted platforms like npm and GitHub highlight the challenges in detection and response.

doc_summary: The incident involves a malicious npm package campaign orchestrated by the North Korean threat actor Famous Chollima, also known as Shifty Corsair. The campaign, codenamed PromptMink, targets the open-source ecosystem, specifically npm and PyPI repositories, to compromise developer systems and steal sensitive data. The attack leverages a layered package strategy, using first-layer packages to import second-layer malicious packages. The primary malicious package, '@validate-sdk/v2', was introduced as a dependency in a project involving Anthropic's Claude Opus large language model. The campaign employs techniques such as typosquatting and transitive dependencies to evade detection. The malware is capable of exfiltrating cryptocurrency wallet credentials and deploying remote access trojans. The attack has evolved to include Rust-compiled payloads and SSH backdoors, demonstrating the threat actor's sophistication and adaptability. The campaign also involves social engineering tactics, using fake companies and job interviews to lure developers into downloading malicious packages.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved a critical RCE vulnerability in GitHub's internal git infrastructure, exploited by adversaries to execute arbitrary commands. The capability was enabled by a delimiter injection in the X-Stat header, allowing attackers to override security policies. GitHub's infrastructure was targeted, affecting repositories and sensitive data. The victim was GitHub's internal infrastructure and potentially all users of GitHub Enterprise Server and GitHub.com.
doc_summary: Wiz Research identified a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, CVE-2026-3854, in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. This high-severity flaw allowed authenticated users to execute arbitrary commands on backend servers using a git push command. The vulnerability stemmed from improper neutralization of special elements during repository push operations. GitHub's architecture processes git push commands using multiple services, passing security-critical metadata via an internal header named X-Stat. The primary entry service, babeld, copied user-controlled git push options into this header without sanitizing semicolon characters, enabling attackers to inject metadata fields. The internal header parsing mechanism's last-write-wins policy allowed attackers to override security policies. Exploitation required chaining three field injections, leading to unsandboxed code execution under the git service user's privileges. On GitHub Enterprise Server, this resulted in complete server compromise, granting unauthorized access to repositories, configuration data, and secrets. On GitHub.com, the multi-tenant architecture increased risk, allowing attackers filesystem access to shared storage nodes. Wiz researchers used AI-augmented reverse-engineering tools to reconstruct internal protocols. GitHub mitigated the vulnerability on GitHub.com within six hours. Immediate patching is required in self-hosted environments.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with the exploitation of a delimiter injection vulnerability in GitHub's X-Stat header, leading to remote code execution. The adversary gained initial access by exploiting CVE-2026-3854, allowing them to execute arbitrary commands and access sensitive data. The attack required chaining specific field injections to bypass security policies and achieve their objectives.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of CVE-2026-3854, a critical vulnerability in GitHub's infrastructure. doc_summary: LofyGang, a Brazilian cybercrime group, has resurfaced after three years, targeting Minecraft players with LofyStealer malware disguised as a Minecraft hack called 'Slinky'. The group uses typosquatted npm packages to distribute the malware, aiming to steal credit card data and user accounts linked to Discord Nitro, gaming, and streaming services. The malware executes a JavaScript loader to deploy LofyStealer, which harvests sensitive data from web browsers and exfiltrates it to a C2 server at 24.152.36[.]241. The group has shifted to a malware-as-a-service model, using GitHub to host repositories for malware families like SmartLoader and Vidar Stealer. This campaign highlights the abuse of trusted platforms for distributing malicious payloads.
